# Backend platform and first read Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build the platform module of the core (errors, security, tenancy, the clock, logs), PostgreSQL with tenants kept apart by the database itself, the migration job, the `workspace` module with `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/shell`, and the `integration` check on a real PostgreSQL and a real Keycloak, each rule proven red by its counter-tests.
**Architecture:** The core becomes two modules of Spring Modulith: `platform` (named interfaces `web` and `security`, the rest hidden) and `workspace` (`internal/web`, `app`, `domain`, `data`), whose boundaries and layers the architecture check verifies. A token passes Spring Security as an OAuth2 resource server; the transaction manager of the core sets the tenant of its user as the first statement of every transaction, and a forced row-level policy on every table filters the rows. The image runs twice from one compose file: as the migration job, which migrates as the owner of the tables and exits, and as the API, which only validates the migrations and refuses a database that is behind.
**Tech Stack:** Spring Boot 4.1.1 (Spring Security 7.1.1, Flyway 12.4.0, HikariCP 7.0.2, PostgreSQL JDBC 42.7.13, Testcontainers 2.0.5), Spring Modulith 2.1.1, datasource-proxy 1.11.1, PostgreSQL 18.6, Keycloak 26.8.1, Mockito 5.23.0, and the toolchain of plan one.
**Spec:** [the backend skeleton design](../specs/2026-10-14-backend-skeleton-design.md), section 12, the row "Two, the platform and the first read" (steps 3 and 4), with the `integration` check; sections 5.2 to 5.10, 6.1 to 6.3, 7 and 8. It starts from the tree [plan one](2026-10-14-backend-foundation-plan.md) left: `./verify` green on its 13 checks, `./canary all` 58 of 58.

## Global Constraints

- Work in `/Users/mrpo/projects/metis/metis-backend`; every path and command of a task is relative to it, and nothing is created outside `/Users/mrpo/projects/metis`.
- Every shell that runs Gradle, `./verify` or `./canary` first runs `export GRADLE_USER_HOME=/Users/mrpo/projects/metis/.work/gradle JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21`.
- Nothing is installed system-wide: no Homebrew, no sudo. Docker Desktop answers on `/var/run/docker.sock`; Testcontainers finds it with no setting. Colima stays stopped.
- Every Gradle command of a task runs as `./gradlew --console=plain --max-workers=5 ...`, half of this machine's ten cores; the integration tests run in one JVM, so their containers and their contexts of Spring start once.
- One heavy job at a time: a Gradle build, a PIT run, a Docker build, the integration tests or a counter-test.
- An Expected block holds lines of the trial run's output. Its seconds, seeds, tree stamps, ports and memory are what that run measured; a new run prints its own, and the rest of each line must match.
- Never run `git add`, `git commit` or `git push`: the last step of each task adds its files to the ledger, and the owner commits.
- The core has two modules of Spring Modulith, each a package under `dev.metis.core`: `platform`, which may use no module and exposes the named interfaces `web` (the exceptions a module throws) and `security` (`CurrentUser`), and `workspace`, which may use those two alone. A module keeps its code in `internal/web`, `internal/app`, `internal/domain` and `internal/data`.
- Every version is written once: in `gradle/libs.versions.toml` (Spring Modulith 2.1.1, datasource-proxy 1.11.1), in Spring Boot 4.1.1's own list, or in `stack/compose.yaml`, which pins `postgres:18.6` and `quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.8.1` by digest; the integration tests read both images and the realm from the stack's own files, so the stack and the tests share one source.
- No password and no client secret in a committed file: the compose file reads each from the environment as `${NAME:?...}`, the realm reads the password of its person as `${METIS_PERSON_PASSWORD}`, and the tests and the image check make a random value for each run.
- Tenants are kept apart by the database: every table holds `tenant_id uuid not null default nullif(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid`, row-level security enabled and forced, the one policy `tenant_rows` on that expression, and a foreign key that names the tenant. The stack's init script `stack/postgres/roles.sh` creates `metis_migrator`, which owns the tables, and `metis_app`, which owns nothing and cannot bypass a policy; a migration grants and never creates a role. The API connects as `metis_app`, holds no password of `metis_migrator` or of the superuser, and only ever reads; the role reads the tables of the registry and the history of the migrations, by any grant and as a member of no role, and every relation it can read is a table that forces row-level security.
- `TenantTransactionManager`, a `JdbcTransactionManager` with `enforceReadOnly` on, declared as a bean that takes the settings Spring Boot gives a transaction manager, runs `select set_config('app.tenant_id', ?, true)` in `prepareTransactionalConnection`, from the `CurrentUser` of the security context; a use case is the only place a transaction starts, by annotation or by any transaction API.
- Bearer tokens only: no session, no cookie, no CSRF token. A token is checked for its signature, issuer, audience `metis-core`, an expiry it must have, and its time by the time of the machine, whatever date the core is fixed at; one UUID in `tenant_id`, in either case, alone or as the one value of a list, and a subject, or 401; a subject the tenant does not know, or a person who is no member of the workspace, 403; a workspace the tenant does not have, 404, by the same path as one that does not exist. Every answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store`; every error is `application/problem+json` with `type`, `title`, `status`, `kind` and `correlationId`, and nothing else.
- Public ids are text keys; a UUID key never leaves the database.
- SQL lives in the repositories of `internal/data` as text blocks with named parameters through `JdbcClient`; only a repository and the tenant hook reach the database, the text of every statement is a string constant of its class, and a repository calls nothing but `JdbcClient` and holds no decision. The repositories and the tenant hook are the only two entries of `config/mutation-exclusions.txt`, each with its reason and counted in `config/debt.json`; the integration tests prove them and never run under PIT.
- The business date is the clock bean of `platform.time.internal`, which `metis.time.fixed` stops under the profile `demo` or `test` alone, and a start with it under any other profile fails; the tests that fix the date run under `test`, which needs no file of its own.
- Every process the tool runs ends at a deadline of 30 minutes with every process it started, and its check is red as timed out; the integration task fails after 20 minutes; no test waits without a limit.
- The bars of plan one hold: 100% of the lines and branches of `core` (the unit and the integration tests together) and `tools`; every PIT mutant detected, and a full run red for a project with code and no mutant; no test skipped; the tests that pass equal `test-floor.json` exactly; every check has a counter-test; English code, comments that say why, `ponytail:` on a deliberate shortcut, no abstraction without a second user.
- Out of this plan: the `delivery` module, `project_member`, `wbs_node` and the overview; the contract file, springdoc, the declaration annotation, the `contract` and `trace` checks; the demo data, the equality with the app's mock data, the restated-literal rule; the rule that `platform` code has two users; the relay; calls generated from the contract; the latency budget; the stop during a slow request.

## Review Focus

The five failure modes the spec implies that are easiest to miss, most likely first. Each is pinned by a test of the task that owns the code; a reviewer checks that the test still fails when the guard it names is removed.

1. A tenant that outlives its transaction on a pooled connection, because the setting was made for the session, so the next transaction of another request sees the rows of the first tenant. Pinned by `TenantTransactionTest.theTenantEndsWithTheTransaction` (Task 5), which first proves that both transactions ran on one connection, and by the counter-test integration-session-tenant.
2. A table a later migration adds without its tenant column, its forced policy or a foreign key that names the tenant, or a view the API can read: the API would still pass every test of the existing tables. Pinned by `CatalogTest` (Task 4), which reads the catalog of the migrated database, and by the counter-tests integration-no-policy, integration-no-force, integration-no-tenant-column and integration-readable-view.
3. A workspace of another tenant answered otherwise than a missing one, by its status, its body or the number of its statements, which tells a caller that the key exists elsewhere. Pinned by `CrossTenantTest.aForeignRecordIsAMissingOne` and `CrossTenantTest.everyEndpointHasItsCases` (Task 6), which fails an endpoint added without its entry in `Endpoints`.
4. Keys of the issuer that cannot be read let `JwtDecoderInitializationException` out of the filters of Spring Security, which answer 401 only for a bad token, so the request failed with 500. Pinned by `TokensTest.keysThatCannotBeReadRejectTheTokenSoTheAnswerIs401AndNot500`, `SecurityTest.aTokenWhoseKeysCannotBeReadIs401AndNot500` (Task 3) and `FailureTest.whenTheKeysOfTheIssuerCannotBeReadATokenIsAnswered401AndNever500` (Task 4).
5. An API that starts on a database the migration job never migrated, or that migrates it itself. Pinned by `MigrationCheckTest` and `StartupTest.theApiRefusesADatabaseTheMigrationJobNeverMigrated` (Task 4), by the step of the image check that starts the API alone on an empty database, and by the counter-test image-unchecked-database.

**State of the blocks:** the whole-file blocks and the Expected outputs of the tasks below show the tree as built after review round one (`./verify` stamp `99fc5f7d9567`). `metis-backend` holds that tree with the changes of review round two; the sections "Review round one" and "Review round two", after Task 10, list what each round changed, file by file.

### Task 1: The integration check

The source set `integrationTest` of the core, for the tests on a real PostgreSQL and a real Keycloak: its own folder `core/src/integrationTest/java`, the shared `test-support` too, so the test of the random order and the guard against calls that leave the machine run there as well, and the versions and the libraries of the core through `implementation` and `runtimeOnly`. Its task runs in one JVM and from the root of the repository, since the tests read the files of the stack; those files are inputs of the task, so a changed stack runs the tests again where a cached result would stand in, and the task fails after twenty minutes rather than hold a check. The check `integration` runs it and the judge of plan one reads its reports against the floor; coverage of the core merges the data of both test tasks. No container yet: the first tests that need one come with the database.

**Files:**

- Create: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/IntegrationCanaries.java`
- Modify: `core/build.gradle.kts`
- Modify: `build.gradle.kts`
- Modify: `tools/build.gradle.kts`
- Modify: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/Canaries.java`
- Modify: `test-floor.json`
- Generated by a command of this task: `core/gradle.lockfile`, `gradle/verification-metadata.xml`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: the conventions of plan one; `TestOrderTest` and the network guard in `test-support`; the command `tests` of the tool; `Checks.ORDER`, which lists `integration` already.
- Produces: the source set and the task `:core:integrationTest`; the root task `checkIntegration` and its judge `:tools:judgeIntegration`; the counter-tests integration-fixed-order and integration-floor.

`core/build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
import java.time.Duration

plugins {
    id("metis.java-conventions")
    alias(libs.plugins.spring.boot)
    alias(libs.plugins.license.report)
}

// The tests on a real PostgreSQL and a real Keycloak, apart from the tests that need no container.
val integrationTest = sourceSets.create("integrationTest") {
    java.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/java"))
    // The architecture rules run with the unit tests alone, and need ArchUnit, which these lack.
    java.exclude("**/ArchitectureRules.java")
    resources.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/resources"))
    compileClasspath += sourceSets.main.get().output
    runtimeClasspath += sourceSets.main.get().output
}

// As the unit tests do, so the versions and the libraries of the core hold for them too.
configurations[integrationTest.implementationConfigurationName].extendsFrom(configurations.implementation.get())
configurations[integrationTest.runtimeOnlyConfigurationName].extendsFrom(configurations.runtimeOnly.get())

dependencies {
    implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc")
    runtimeOnly("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-actuator")
    testImplementation(libs.archunit)
    testImplementation("org.awaitility:awaitility")
    testImplementation("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-params")
    testImplementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test")
    "integrationTestImplementation"(platform(libs.junit.bom))
    "integrationTestImplementation"("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api")
    "integrationTestImplementation"("org.assertj:assertj-core")
    "integrationTestCompileOnly"("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    "integrationTestRuntimeOnly"("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-engine")
    "integrationTestRuntimeOnly"("org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher")
}

val integrationTestTask = tasks.register<Test>("integrationTest") {
    description = "Runs the tests on a real PostgreSQL and a real Keycloak."
    testClassesDirs = integrationTest.output.classesDirs
    classpath = integrationTest.runtimeClasspath
    // One JVM, so the containers and the contexts of Spring start once for every class.
    maxParallelForks = 1
    // The tests read the stack's own files, so the stack and the tests share one source.
    workingDir = rootDir
    // Those files are inputs, so a changed stack runs the tests again and no cached result stands in.
    inputs.dir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("stack")).withPathSensitivity(PathSensitivity.RELATIVE)
    // A test that would wait for ever fails the check after this instead of holding it.
    timeout = Duration.ofMinutes(20)
}

// Coverage counts the lines both test tasks run, since only a database runs a repository.
tasks.jacocoTestReport {
    dependsOn(integrationTestTask)
    executionData(tasks.test.get(), integrationTestTask.get())
}

tasks.register<Test>("deadcodeTest") {
    description = "Runs the test that every setting of application.yml is one that something defines."
    testClassesDirs = sourceSets.test.get().output.classesDirs
    classpath = sourceSets.test.get().runtimeClasspath
    useJUnitPlatform {
        includeTags("deadcode")
    }
}

licenseReport {
    configurations = arrayOf("runtimeClasspath")
    filters = arrayOf(com.github.jk1.license.filter.SpdxLicenseBundleNormalizer())
    allowedLicensesFile = rootProject.file("config/allowed-licenses.json")
}
```

`build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
plugins {
    alias(libs.plugins.spotless)
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
}

spotless {
    java {
        target("core/src/**/*.java", "tools/src/**/*.java", "test-support/**/*.java")
        googleJavaFormat(libs.versions.google.java.format.get())
        removeUnusedImports()
    }
    format("misc") {
        target(
            "**/*.kts", "**/*.md", "**/*.yml", "**/*.yaml", "**/*.toml", "**/*.properties",
            "**/*.json", "**/*.xml", "**/*.txt", "**/Dockerfile", "**/.gitignore", ".dockerignore",
            "verify", "canary",
        )
        targetExclude("**/build/**", "**/.gradle/**", "**/.kotlin/**", "gradle/verification-metadata.xml")
        trimTrailingWhitespace()
        endWithNewline()
    }
}

// A scanner that is no Gradle plugin, run as its pinned image in the tree, which it reads only.
fun scanner(name: String, image: Provider<String>, options: List<String>, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<Exec>(name) {
        val tree = rootDir.absolutePath
        commandLine(
            listOf("docker", "run", "--rm", "--volume", "$tree:/work:ro", "--workdir", "/work") +
                options + listOf(image.get()) + arguments,
        )
    }

// Trivy keeps its database in a volume of its own, so a scan downloads it once a day at most.
val trivy = listOf("--volume", "metis-trivy-cache:/root/.cache")

scanner(
    "depsVulnerabilities", libs.versions.image.trivy, trivy,
    "fs", "--scanners", "vuln", "--exit-code", "1", "--quiet",
    "--skip-dirs", "/work/build", "--skip-dirs", "/work/**/build", "--skip-dirs", "/work/.gradle", "/work",
)

// A relative folder, so the paths the allow-list of .gitleaks.toml matches start at the root.
scanner(
    "secretsScan", libs.versions.image.gitleaks, listOf(),
    "dir", ".", "--no-banner", "--redact", "--verbose", "--config", ".gitleaks.toml",
)

// actionlint finds the workflows through .git, which the copy of a canary lacks, so each is named.
val workflows = file(".github/workflows").list().orEmpty().sorted().map { ".github/workflows/$it" }

scanner("workflowLint", libs.versions.image.actionlint, listOf(), "-color", *workflows.toTypedArray())

// The image the image check builds from the sources, with Docker alone, as any platform would.
tasks.register<Exec>("imageBuild") {
    commandLine("docker", "build", "--file", "core/Dockerfile", "--tag", "metis-core:check", ".")
}

tasks.register<Exec>("imageLint") {
    val dockerfile = file("core/Dockerfile")
    commandLine("docker", "run", "--rm", "--interactive", libs.versions.image.hadolint.get(), "hadolint", "-")
    doFirst {
        standardInput = dockerfile.inputStream()
    }
}

// Trivy reads the image from an archive in the tree, so it needs no hand on the Docker daemon.
tasks.register<Exec>("imageSave") {
    dependsOn("imageBuild")
    val archive = layout.buildDirectory.file("image/core.tar")
    doFirst {
        archive.get().asFile.parentFile.mkdirs()
    }
    commandLine("docker", "save", "--output", archive.get().asFile.path, "metis-core:check")
}

scanner(
    "imageScan", libs.versions.image.trivy, trivy,
    "image", "--input", "/work/build/image/core.tar", "--scanners", "vuln", "--exit-code", "1", "--quiet",
).configure { dependsOn("imageSave") }

// The checks of ./verify, which runs them in the order of the list of the tool, Checks.ORDER.

tasks.register("checkFormat") {
    description = "Every source file is formatted."
    dependsOn("spotlessCheck")
}

tasks.register("checkCompile") {
    description = "The code compiles with every warning an error, no bug pattern and no null where none is allowed."
    dependsOn(
        ":core:compileJava", ":core:compileTestJava", ":core:compileIntegrationTestJava",
        ":tools:compileJava", ":tools:compileTestJava",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkLint") {
    description = "No method above a complexity of 10, no file above 300 lines, a reason on every mark."
    dependsOn(
        ":core:checkstyleMain", ":core:checkstyleTest", ":core:checkstyleIntegrationTest",
        ":tools:checkstyleMain", ":tools:checkstyleTest", ":tools:marks",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkLanguage") {
    description = "English only, and no comment that cites a plan, a ruling, a task, a date or a line of a file."
    dependsOn(":tools:language")
}

tasks.register("checkArchitecture") {
    description = "The architecture rules of both projects hold."
    dependsOn(":core:architectureTest", ":tools:architectureTest", ":tools:judgeArchitecture")
}

tasks.register("checkDeadcode") {
    description = "Nothing unused: code, test helpers, dependencies and settings."
    dependsOn(
        ":core:projectHealth", ":tools:projectHealth", "bundledDeclared", ":tools:deadcode",
        ":core:deadcodeTest", ":tools:judgeDeadcode",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkTooling") {
    description = "The tests of the tool pass, every check has a counter-test, the workflow passes its linter."
    dependsOn(":tools:test", ":tools:judgeTooling", "workflowLint")
}

tasks.register("checkUnit") {
    description = "The tests of the core that need no container pass, none skipped, as many as the floor."
    dependsOn(":core:test", ":tools:judgeUnit")
}

tasks.register("checkIntegration") {
    description = "The tests on a real PostgreSQL and a real Keycloak pass, none skipped, as many as the floor."
    dependsOn(":core:integrationTest", ":tools:judgeIntegration")
}

tasks.register("checkCoverage") {
    description = "Every line and every branch of the core and the tool runs in a test."
    dependsOn(":core:jacocoTestReport", ":tools:jacocoTestReport", ":tools:judgeCoverage")
}

tasks.register("checkMutation") {
    description = "Every mutant PIT makes of the core and the tool is killed by a test."
    dependsOn(":core:pitest", ":tools:pitest", ":tools:judgeMutation")
}

tasks.register("checkDeps") {
    description = "No known vulnerability, only allowed licences, and current lock files and checksums."
    dependsOn("depsVulnerabilities", ":core:checkLicense", ":core:resolveLocked", ":tools:resolveLocked")
}

tasks.register("checkSecrets") {
    description = "No secret in the tree."
    dependsOn("secretsScan")
}

tasks.register("checkImage") {
    description = "The image builds from the sources, passes its linter and its scan, and runs locked down."
    dependsOn("imageLint", "imageBuild", "imageScan", ":tools:imageRun")
}

// A check whose judge did not run would pass on the exit of its tasks alone, so a check that owes
// facts fails without them; ./verify and ./canary clear the facts before each run of a check.
val factFree = setOf("checkFormat", "checkCompile", "checkDeps", "checkSecrets")
tasks.matching { it.name.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) && it.name !in factFree }.configureEach {
    val check = name.removePrefix("check").replaceFirstChar(Char::lowercase)
    val facts = layout.buildDirectory.file("facts/$check.txt")
    doLast {
        if (!facts.get().asFile.exists()) {
            throw GradleException("$name: its judge left no facts in build/facts/$check.txt")
        }
    }
}

// A starter stands for the libraries of it that the code uses, named one by one, which the plugin
// would otherwise ask to declare; a library a bundle names is never reported unused, so
// bundledDeclared refuses a project that declares one of them itself.
val starters =
    mapOf(
        "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc" to listOf(
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-autoconfigure",
            "org.springframework:spring-context",
        ),
        "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test" to listOf(
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-resttestclient",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-test",
            "org.springframework:spring-beans",
            "org.springframework:spring-core",
            "org.springframework:spring-test",
            "org.springframework:spring-web",
        ),
    )

configure<com.autonomousapps.DependencyAnalysisExtension> {
    structure {
        starters.forEach { (starter, libraries) ->
            bundle(starter.substringAfter(':')) {
                primary(starter)
                libraries.forEach { includeDependency(it) }
            }
        }
    }
    issues {
        all {
            onAny {
                severity("fail")
            }
        }
    }
}

val bundled = tasks.register("bundledDeclared") {
    description = "No project declares a library that a bundle names."
}

gradle.projectsEvaluated {
    val members = starters.values.flatten().toSet()
    val declared =
        subprojects.flatMap { project ->
            project.configurations.flatMap { configuration ->
                configuration.dependencies
                    .filter { "${it.group}:${it.name}" in members }
                    .map { "${it.group}:${it.name} in ${project.path} ${configuration.name}" }
            }
        }
    bundled.configure {
        doLast {
            if (declared.isNotEmpty()) {
                throw GradleException("a bundle names what a project declares, which it would never report: $declared")
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("metis.java-conventions")
    application
}

application {
    mainClass = "dev.metis.tools.Main"
}

dependencies {
    implementation(libs.archunit)
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-core")
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind")
}

// A command of the tool, run from the repository root, for a check of the root build to depend on.
fun tool(name: String, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<JavaExec>(name) {
        classpath = sourceSets.main.get().runtimeClasspath
        mainClass = application.mainClass
        workingDir = rootDir
        args(*arguments)
    }

tool("language", "language")
tool("marks", "marks")
// The walk resolves the types the classes of both projects extend, so it runs on their classpaths.
evaluationDependsOn(":core")
tool("deadcode", "deadcode", "config/entry-points.txt", "core", "tools").configure {
    val core = project(":core").the<SourceSetContainer>()
    classpath += core["test"].runtimeClasspath + sourceSets.test.get().runtimeClasspath
    dependsOn(":core:testClasses", tasks.testClasses)
}
// The judges of the test tasks, which run after the tests even when a test failed.
tool("judgeArchitecture", "tests", "architecture", "core/build/test-results/architectureTest", "tools/build/test-results/architectureTest")
    .configure { mustRunAfter(":core:architectureTest", tasks.named("architectureTest")) }
tool("judgeDeadcode", "tests", "deadcode", "core/build/test-results/deadcodeTest")
    .configure { mustRunAfter(":core:deadcodeTest") }
tool(
    "judgeCoverage", "coverage", "core/build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml",
    "tools/build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml",
).configure { mustRunAfter(":core:jacocoTestReport", tasks.jacocoTestReport) }
// What PIT mutates: the classes of -Pmutate, else the classes changed since MUTATION_BASE, else all.
tool("mutationScope", "mutation-scope").configure {
    val given = providers.gradleProperty("mutate").map { listOf("--given", it) }
    val base = providers.environmentVariable("MUTATION_BASE").filter { it.isNotBlank() }.map { listOf("--base", it) }
    argumentProviders.add(CommandLineArgumentProvider { given.orElse(base).getOrElse(listOf()) + listOf("core", "tools") })
}
tool("judgeMutation", "mutation", "core", "tools").configure { mustRunAfter(":core:pitest", tasks.pitest) }
tool("imageRun", "image", "metis-core:check").configure { dependsOn(":imageBuild") }
tool("judgeTooling", "tests", "tooling", "tools/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(tasks.test) }
tool("judgeUnit", "tests", "unit", "core/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(":core:test") }
tool("judgeIntegration", "tests", "integration", "core/build/test-results/integrationTest")
    .configure { mustRunAfter(":core:integrationTest") }

// ./verify and ./canary start the tool with the Java and the classpath this task writes, and the tool
// learns from it the check tasks Gradle has in every project, however a build file declares them.
val launcher = tasks.register("launcher") {
    val executable = javaToolchains.launcherFor(java.toolchain).map { it.executablePath.asFile.path }
    val classpath = sourceSets.main.map { it.runtimeClasspath }
    val checks = rootProject.allprojects.flatMap { project ->
        val prefix = if (project == rootProject) "" else project.path + ":"
        project.tasks.names.filter { it.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) }.map { prefix + it }
    }
    val folder = layout.buildDirectory.dir("launcher")
    inputs.files(classpath)
    inputs.property("java", executable)
    inputs.property("checks", checks)
    outputs.dir(folder)
    doLast {
        folder.get().file("java").asFile.writeText(executable.get() + "\n")
        folder.get().file("args").asFile.writeText("-cp\n\"" + classpath.get().asPath + "\"\n")
        folder.get().file("checks").asFile.writeText(checks.joinToString("") { "$it\n" })
    }
}

// The tests of the counter-tests read the list of checks the launcher writes.
tasks.named("testClasses") { dependsOn(launcher) }
```

### Task 2: The walk knows what Spring calls, and the titles of tests are read as comments

The deadcode walk of plan one starts from a list of entry points. The core is about to have beans, controllers and settings that Spring alone calls, so the walk takes three more kinds of root: the constructors of what Spring makes (a class marked `@Component`, or above it, and a record of `@ConfigurationProperties`), the methods Spring calls (mapped to a request, a handler of exceptions, a bean, a listener), and the accessors of the records an answer of a mapped method holds, which Jackson reads. A record a class literal names is made by reflection, as a row of a query, so its constructors are used; the attributes of an annotation are set wherever it stands. A method the test context of Spring calls, such as one marked `@DynamicPropertySource`, is a root of the tests, and the serialization of the JDK reads the `serialVersionUID` of a serializable class, however few classes name it. The tests of every source set but main walk together, so a helper of the unit tests may serve the integration tests. The tests that prove a requirement open their `@DisplayName` with its BRD id, so the language check reads a title as it reads a comment.

**Files:**

- Test: `tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/deadcode/WalkReflectionTest.java`
- Modify: `tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/deadcode/DeadcodeTest.java`
- Modify: `tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/language/LanguageTest.java`
- Modify: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/deadcode/Walk.java`
- Modify: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/deadcode/Deadcode.java`
- Modify: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/language/Comments.java`
- Modify: `tools/build.gradle.kts`
- Modify: `config/entry-points.txt`
- Modify: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/DeadcodeCanaries.java`
- Modify: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/LanguageCanaries.java`
- Modify: `test-floor.json`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: `Walk`, `Deadcode`, `Comments` of plan one; `Samples` and `WalkTest.unused` of its tests.
- Produces: `Walk.SPRING` (`Predicate<JavaMember>`), the test sets of `Deadcode` (every folder of `<project>/build/classes/java` but `main`), the titles of `Comments.of`, the classpath of the task `:tools:deadcode` with the integration tests; the counter-tests deadcode-bean-method and language-test-title.

```java
package dev.metis.tools.deadcode;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

// What a framework calls by reflection, which no call in the class files shows.
class WalkReflectionTest {

  @TempDir Path dir;

  // An annotation of the samples, named as Spring names its own, which the walk reads by name.
  private static String annotation(String name, String above) {
    int dot = name.lastIndexOf('.');
    return "package %s; %s @java.lang.annotation.Retention(java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME) public @interface %s {}"
        .formatted(name.substring(0, dot), above, name.substring(dot + 1));
  }

  @Test
  void whatSpringMakesOrCallsIsUsedAndTheRecordsOfAMappedAnswerAreWrittenWhole() {
    Map<String, String> files = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    for (String name :
        List.of(
            "org.springframework.stereotype.Component",
            "org.springframework.boot.context.properties.ConfigurationProperties",
            "org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping",
            "org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ExceptionHandler",
            "org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean",
            "org.springframework.context.event.EventListener")) {
      files.put(name.replace('.', '/') + ".java", annotation(name, ""));
    }
    files.put(
        "org/springframework/web/bind/annotation/GetMapping.java",
        annotation("org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping", "@RequestMapping"));
    files.put("s/Rest.java", annotation("s.Rest", "@org.springframework.stereotype.Component"));
    files.put(
        "s/Shop.java",
        """
        package s;
        @Rest class Shop {
          private final Stock stock;
          Shop(Stock stock) { this.stock = stock; }
          @org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping
          Answer answer() {
            return new Answer(stock.count(), java.util.List.of(new Line("a", java.util.List.of())), new Box());
          }
          Note note() { return new Note("n"); }
          void idle() {}
        }
        """);
    files.put(
        "s/Stock.java",
        """
        package s;
        @org.springframework.stereotype.Component
        class Stock {
          int count() { return new Shop(this).note() == null ? 0 : 1; }
          int unused() { return 2; }
        }
        """);
    files.put(
        "s/Answer.java",
        """
        package s;
        record Answer(int count, java.util.List<Line> lines, Box box) {
          static final String label = "answer";
          static String label() { return label; }
          int extra() { return count + 1; }
        }
        """);
    files.put("s/Line.java", "package s; record Line(String text, java.util.List<Line> more) {}");
    files.put("s/Note.java", "package s; record Note(String text) {}");
    // A class, not a record, whose method is named as its field: Jackson does not read it.
    files.put(
        "s/Box.java",
        "package s; class Box { private final int size = 1; int size() { return size; } }");
    files.put(
        "s/Spare.java",
        """
        package s;
        @org.springframework.stereotype.Component
        class Spare {
          @org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean Stock stock() { return new Stock(); }
          @org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ExceptionHandler String failed() { return "x"; }
          @org.springframework.context.event.EventListener void started() {}
        }
        """);
    files.put(
        "s/Settings.java",
        """
        package s;
        @org.springframework.boot.context.properties.ConfigurationProperties
        record Settings(String name) {}
        """);
    files.put("s/Plain.java", "package s; class Plain { Plain(int size) {} }");
    assertThat(
            new Walk(Samples.compile(dir, files))
                .from(Walk.SPRING)
                .unused(String.join("\n", files.values())))
        .containsExactly(
            "class s.Plain",
            "method s.Answer.extra()",
            "method s.Answer.label()",
            "method s.Box.size()",
            "method s.Note.text()",
            "method s.Settings.name()",
            "method s.Shop.idle()",
            "method s.Stock.unused()");
  }

  @Test
  void aRecordAClassLiteralNamesIsMadeAndTheAttributesOfAnAnnotationAreSet() {
    assertThat(
            WalkTest.unused(
                dir,
                WalkTest.MAIN,
                """
                @Tagged(name = "app") class App {
                  public static void main(String[] a) { System.out.println(Row.class + " " + Plain.class); }
                }
                """,
                "@java.lang.annotation.Retention(java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME) @interface Tagged { String name(); }",
                "record Row(int size) {}",
                "record Kept(int size) {}",
                "class Plain { Plain(int size) {} }"))
        .containsExactly("class s.Kept", "constructor s.Plain.<init>(int)", "method s.Row.size()");
  }

  @Test
  void whatTheTestContextOfSpringCallsIsUsed() {
    String name = "org.springframework.test.context.DynamicPropertySource";
    Map<String, String> files = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    files.put(name.replace('.', '/') + ".java", annotation(name, ""));
    files.put(
        "s/ATest.java",
        """
        package s;
        class ATest {
          @org.springframework.test.context.DynamicPropertySource static void settings() {}
          static void idle() {}
        }
        """);
    assertThat(
            new Walk(Samples.compile(dir, files))
                .from(Walk.TESTS)
                .unused(String.join("\n", files.values())))
        .containsExactly("method s.ATest.idle()");
  }

  @Test
  void theSerializationOfTheJdkReadsTheVersionOfASerializableClassAlone() {
    String main =
        "class App { public static void main(String[] a) { System.out.println(new %s()); } }";
    String version = "private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;";
    assertThat(
            WalkTest.unused(
                dir.resolve("kept"),
                WalkTest.MAIN,
                main.formatted("Kept"),
                "class Kept implements java.io.Serializable { " + version + " }"))
        .isEmpty();
    assertThat(
            WalkTest.unused(
                dir.resolve("loose"),
                WalkTest.MAIN,
                main.formatted("Loose"),
                "class Loose { " + version + " }"))
        .containsExactly("field s.Loose.serialVersionUID");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.deadcode;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.metis.tools.TestContext;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class DeadcodeTest {

  private static final String APP =
      "package s; public class App { public static void main(String[] a) { Used.run(); } }";
  private static final String USED =
      """
      package s;
      public class Used {
        static final String NAME = "used";
        static void run() { System.out.println(NAME); }
        public static void idle() {}
      }
      """;
  private static final String TEST =
      """
      package s;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
      class UsedTest { @Test void runs() { Used.run(); Helper.help(); } }
      """;
  private static final String HELPER = "package s; class Helper { static void help() {} }";
  private static final String ORPHAN = "package s; class Orphan { static void help() {} }";

  @TempDir Path root;

  // A project with its sources under src and its classes where Gradle writes them.
  private void project(String name, Map<String, String> main, Map<String, String> tests)
      throws IOException {
    write(name + "/src/main/java", main);
    write(name + "/src/test/java", tests);
    Samples.compile(root.resolve(name + "/build/classes/java/main"), main);
    if (!tests.isEmpty()) {
      Path classes = root.resolve(name + "/build/classes/java/test");
      Samples.compile(classes, tests, root.resolve(name + "/build/classes/java/main"));
    }
  }

  private void write(String folder, Map<String, String> sources) throws IOException {
    for (Map.Entry<String, String> source : sources.entrySet()) {
      Path file = root.resolve(folder).resolve(source.getKey());
      Files.createDirectories(file.getParent());
      Files.writeString(file, source.getValue());
    }
  }

  private TestContext walk(String entries) throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("config"));
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("config/entry-points.txt"), entries);
    TestContext test = new TestContext(root);
    test.exit = Deadcode.command(test.context(), List.of("config/entry-points.txt", "core"));
    return test;
  }

  @Test
  void theProductionWalkStartsFromTheListAndTheTestWalkFromTheTests() throws IOException {
    project(
        "core",
        Map.of("s/App.java", APP, "s/Used.java", USED),
        Map.of("s/UsedTest.java", TEST, "s/Helper.java", HELPER, "s/Orphan.java", ORPHAN));
    TestContext test = walk("# Entry points.\n\ns.App.main: started by the JVM\n");
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "core: method s.Used.idle() is never used",
            "core tests: class s.Orphan is never used",
            "deadcode: 2 problems");
  }

  @Test
  void aClassOfTheListIsUsedWholeAndTheCountAddsTheClassesBothWalksReached() throws IOException {
    project(
        "core",
        Map.of("s/App.java", APP, "s/Used.java", USED),
        Map.of("s/UsedTest.java", TEST, "s/Helper.java", HELPER));
    TestContext test = walk("s.App.main: started by the JVM\ns.Used: read by reflection\n");
    assertThat(test.exit).isZero();
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("deadcode: clean (4 classes reached)\n");
  }

  @Test
  void theTestsOfEverySourceSetButMainWalkTogetherAndSpringFindsItsOwnRoots() throws IOException {
    String component = "package org.springframework.stereotype; public @interface Component {}";
    String bean =
        "package s; @org.springframework.stereotype.Component public class Bean {"
            + " public Bean() {} public Bean(int size) {} }";
    project(
        "core",
        Map.of(
            "s/App.java",
            APP,
            "s/Used.java",
            USED,
            "s/Bean.java",
            bean,
            "org/springframework/stereotype/Component.java",
            component),
        Map.of("s/Helper.java", HELPER));
    Map<String, String> more = Map.of("s/UsedTest.java", TEST, "s/Orphan.java", ORPHAN);
    write("core/src/integrationTest/java", more);
    Samples.compile(
        root.resolve("core/build/classes/java/integrationTest"),
        more,
        root.resolve("core/build/classes/java/main"),
        root.resolve("core/build/classes/java/test"));
    TestContext test = walk("s.App.main: started by the JVM\ns.Used.idle: called by a test\n");
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly("core tests: class s.Orphan is never used", "deadcode: 1 problems");
  }

  @Test
  void aProjectWithoutTestsHasOnlyItsProductionWalk() throws IOException {
    project("core", Map.of("s/App.java", APP, "s/Used.java", USED), Map.of());
    TestContext test = walk("s.App.main: started by the JVM\ns.Used: read by reflection\n");
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("deadcode: clean (2 classes reached)\n");
  }

  @Test
  void aProjectNeverBuiltHasNoClassToWalk() throws IOException {
    write("core/src/main/java", Map.of("s/App.java", APP));
    TestContext test = walk("");
    assertThat(test.exit).isZero();
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("deadcode: clean (0 classes reached)\n");
  }

  @Test
  void anEntryWithoutAReasonOrThatNamesNothingIsAProblemOfTheList() throws IOException {
    project("core", Map.of("s/App.java", APP, "s/Used.java", USED), Map.of());
    TestContext test =
        walk("s.App.main\ns.App.main: started\ns.Used: read\ns.Gone.run: removed long ago\n: x\n");
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "config/entry-points.txt:1: no-reason: s.App.main",
            "config/entry-points.txt:5: no-reason: : x",
            "config/entry-points.txt:4: names nothing: s.Gone.run",
            "deadcode: 3 problems");
  }

  @Test
  void withoutAListAndAProjectItPrintsItsUsage() throws IOException {
    TestContext test = new TestContext(root);
    assertThat(Deadcode.command(test.context(), List.of("config/entry-points.txt"))).isEqualTo(2);
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("usage: deadcode <file of entry points> <project> ...\n");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.language;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class LanguageTest {

  // Banned samples are built from pieces and escapes, so this file passes the check it tests.
  private static final String VI = "Ti\u1ebfng Vi\u1ec7t";
  private static final List<String> RULINGS =
      List.of("R-" + "B15", "D-" + "B23", "FE-" + "23", "BK-" + "02", "RD-" + "13", "BE-" + "01");
  private static final List<String> TASKS =
      List.of("Task" + " 13", "Task" + " 6b", "Tasks" + " 3 and 4", "plan" + " two", "Plan" + " B");
  private static final String SPEC = "spec" + " 4.4";
  private static final String LETTER = "non-ascii-letter";
  private static final String MARK = "lang-" + "exception:";

  private static List<String> rules(String path, String text) {
    return Language.scan(path, text).stream()
        .map(problem -> problem.line() + ":" + problem.rule())
        .toList();
  }

  private static List<String> found(String sample) {
    return rules("A.java", "// " + sample + "\n");
  }

  private static void flagged(String rule, List<String> samples) {
    for (String sample : samples) {
      assertThat(found(sample)).as(sample).containsExactly("1:" + rule);
    }
  }

  private static void clean(List<String> samples) {
    for (String sample : samples) {
      assertThat(found(sample)).as(sample).isEmpty();
    }
  }

  @Test
  void flagsEveryLetterOutsideAsciiInAnyCaseOrScriptComposedOrDecomposed() {
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "// " + VI + "\nint a = 1;\n")).containsExactly("1:" + LETTER);
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "String a = \"" + VI + "\";\n")).containsExactly("1:" + LETTER);
    String decomposed = java.text.Normalizer.normalize(VI, java.text.Normalizer.Form.NFD);
    assertThat(decomposed).isNotEqualTo(VI);
    flagged(
        LETTER,
        List.of("Jos\u00e9 M\u00fcller", "\u0110\u00c0 N\u1eb4NG", "\u65e5\u672c", decomposed));
    assertThat(rules("a.yml", "# " + VI + "\n")).containsExactly("1:" + LETTER);
  }

  @Test
  void ignoresPunctuationAndSymbolsThatAreNotLetters() {
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "String a = \"+ 2 \u00b7 seen \u2318 \u00a9\";\n")).isEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void aLangExceptionWithAReasonExcusesTheNextLineAndOnlyTheLetterRule() {
    String text =
        "// " + MARK + " a native name\nString a = \"" + VI + "\";\nString b = \"" + VI + "\";\n";
    assertThat(rules("A.java", text)).containsExactly("3:" + LETTER);
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "// " + MARK + " sample\n// " + RULINGS.getFirst() + "\n"))
        .containsExactly("2:plan-reference");
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "// lang-exception without the colon\nString a = \"" + VI + "\";\n"))
        .containsExactly("2:" + LETTER);
  }

  @Test
  void flagsRulingIdsTaskNumbersAndPlanNamesButKeepsBrdIds() {
    flagged("plan-reference", RULINGS);
    flagged("plan-reference", TASKS);
    flagged("plan-reference", List.of("ruling" + " 14", "Rulings" + " 3"));
    clean(
        List.of(
            "OVW-01 BR-24 D-19",
            "PR-B15 SFE-23 FE-23x Task 5th R-12",
            "a task queue, a plan of the trip"));
  }

  @Test
  void flagsSpecSectionNumbersInEveryForm() {
    flagged(
        "spec-reference",
        List.of(
            SPEC,
            "Spec" + " 3.2",
            "specs" + " 3.2",
            "spec" + " line 71",
            "spec" + " section 4.4",
            "spec" + " \u00a74.4",
            "see \u00a7" + "4.4",
            "per section" + " 4.4",
            "Section" + " 7"));
    clean(List.of("the spec says so", "the section on tiers"));
  }

  @Test
  void flagsALineOfAnotherFileButNotAPortOrAVersion() {
    flagged(
        "file-line",
        List.of(
            "Verify" + ".java:42",
            "see verify" + ".mjs:12",
            "application" + ".yml:3",
            "README" + ".md line 3",
            "a" + ".java lines 3"));
    clean(
        List.of(
            "http://127.0.0.1:8080", "version 1.2.3", "line 4 of the table", "core/Dockerfile"));
  }

  @Test
  void flagsDatesInComments() {
    flagged(
        "date", List.of("measured on 9" + " Oct 2026", "10" + " October 2026", "2026" + "-10-09"));
    clean(List.of("in Oct 2026, 2026-10 and version 2026.10.9"));
  }

  @Test
  void theReferenceRulesReadCommentsOnlySoProductTextInCodeAndDataPasses() {
    String date = "2026" + "-10-09";
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "String a = \"" + TASKS.getFirst() + " " + date + "\";\n"))
        .isEmpty();
    assertThat(rules("a.yml", "name: " + TASKS.getFirst() + "\n")).isEmpty();
    assertThat(rules("a.yml", "name: x # " + TASKS.getFirst() + "\n"))
        .containsExactly("1:plan-reference");
    assertThat(rules("A.md", TASKS.getFirst() + " added this\n"))
        .containsExactly("1:plan-reference");
    assertThat(rules("a.xml", "<a>" + TASKS.getFirst() + "</a> <!-- " + date + " -->\n"))
        .containsExactly("1:date");
  }

  @Test
  void reportsEachBrokenRuleOnceALineWithTheLineTrimmedAndCutAtAHundredCharacters() {
    List<Language.Problem> problems =
        Language.scan(
            "A.java", "   // " + SPEC + " " + RULINGS.getFirst() + " " + "x".repeat(200) + "\n");
    assertThat(problems)
        .extracting(Language.Problem::rule)
        .containsExactly("plan-reference", "spec-reference");
    assertThat(problems.getFirst().excerpt()).hasSize(100).startsWith("// spec");
    assertThat(problems.getFirst().line()).isEqualTo(1);
  }

  @Test
  void theTitleOfATestIsReadLikeAComment() {
    String title = "@Display" + "Name";
    assertThat(rules("ATest.java", title + "(\"as the " + SPEC + " says\")\nvoid a() {}\n"))
        .containsExactly("1:spec-reference");
    assertThat(
            rules("ATest.java", "int a;\n" + title + "(\n    \"done in " + TASKS.get(0) + "\")\n"))
        .containsExactly("3:plan-reference");
    assertThat(rules("ATest.java", title + "(\"TEN-02 a tenant sees \\\"its\\\" rows\")\n"))
        .isEmpty();
    assertThat(rules("a.kts", title + "(\"as the " + SPEC + " says\")\n")).isEmpty();
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.deadcode;

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaAccess;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaAnnotation;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClass;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClasses;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaCodeUnit;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaConstructor;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaField;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaFieldAccess;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaMember;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaMethod;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaModifier;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaParameterizedType;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaType;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.TryCatchBlock;
import java.io.Serializable;
import java.util.ArrayDeque;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Deque;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.function.Predicate;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** A walk over the class files of a project from its roots; what it never reaches is unused. */
final class Walk {

  /** The roots of a walk over tests: the members a test engine or Spring's test context runs. */
  static final Predicate<JavaMember> TESTS =
      member ->
          member.getAnnotations().stream()
              .map(annotation -> annotation.getRawType().getPackageName())
              .anyMatch(
                  name ->
                      name.startsWith("org.junit.")
                          || name.startsWith("com.tngtech.archunit.junit")
                          || name.equals("org.springframework.test.context"));

  // What Spring makes by itself, by an annotation on the class or one above it.
  private static final List<String> MADE =
      List.of(
          "org.springframework.stereotype.Component",
          "org.springframework.boot.context.properties.ConfigurationProperties");

  // What Spring calls by itself: a method mapped to a request, a handler, a bean, a listener.
  private static final String MAPPED = "org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping";
  private static final List<String> CALLED =
      List.of(
          MAPPED,
          "org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ExceptionHandler",
          "org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean",
          "org.springframework.context.event.EventListener");

  /** The roots Spring finds by itself: the constructors of what it makes and what it calls. */
  static final Predicate<JavaMember> SPRING =
      member ->
          member instanceof JavaConstructor
              ? MADE.stream().anyMatch(member.getOwner()::isMetaAnnotatedWith)
              : CALLED.stream().anyMatch(member::isMetaAnnotatedWith);

  private final JavaClasses classes;
  private final Set<JavaClass> types = new HashSet<>();
  private final Set<JavaClass> answers = new HashSet<>();
  private final Set<JavaMember> members = new HashSet<>();
  private final Deque<JavaCodeUnit> pending = new ArrayDeque<>();

  Walk(JavaClasses classes) {
    this.classes = classes;
  }

  /** Walks from every member the predicate names a root. */
  Walk from(Predicate<JavaMember> roots) {
    for (JavaClass type : classes) {
      for (JavaMember member : type.getMembers()) {
        if (roots.test(member)) {
          reach(member);
          // A class that holds a root is made by whatever calls the root, its constructors too.
          type.getConstructors().forEach(this::reach);
        }
      }
    }
    // An override is used once its class is reached and the method above it is, in any order.
    int before;
    do {
      before = members.size();
      while (!pending.isEmpty()) {
        visit(pending.pop());
      }
      for (JavaClass type : List.copyOf(types)) {
        type.getMethods().stream().filter(method -> overrides(type, method)).forEach(this::reach);
      }
    } while (members.size() > before);
    return this;
  }

  /** How many classes of the project the walk reached. */
  int reached() {
    return types.size();
  }

  /** What the walk never reached, as kind and name, in name order; sources hold every name. */
  List<String> unused(String sources) {
    List<String> unused = new ArrayList<>();
    for (JavaClass type : classes) {
      if (!types.contains(type)) {
        if (reportable(type)) {
          unused.add("class " + type.getName());
        }
        continue;
      }
      type.getCodeUnits().stream()
          .filter(unit -> !members.contains(unit) && reportable(unit))
          .forEach(unit -> unused.add(kindOf(unit) + " " + unit.getFullName()));
      type.getFields().stream()
          .filter(field -> unusedField(field, sources))
          .forEach(field -> unused.add("field " + field.getFullName()));
    }
    return unused.stream().sorted().toList();
  }

  private void reach(JavaMember member) {
    if (!members.add(member)) {
      return;
    }
    reachType(member.getOwner());
    if (member instanceof JavaCodeUnit unit) {
      pending.push(unit);
    }
    if (member instanceof JavaField field) {
      reachType(field.getRawType());
    }
    if (member instanceof JavaMethod method && method.isMetaAnnotatedWith(MAPPED)) {
      written(method.getReturnType());
    }
  }

  // Jackson writes the answer of a mapped method through the accessors of its records, unseen.
  private void written(JavaType type) {
    JavaClass raw = type.toErasure();
    if (raw.isRecord() && answers.add(raw)) {
      for (JavaField field : raw.getFields()) {
        if (!field.getModifiers().contains(JavaModifier.STATIC)) {
          raw.tryGetMethod(field.getName()).ifPresent(this::reach);
          written(field.getType());
        }
      }
    }
    if (type instanceof JavaParameterizedType generic) {
      generic.getActualTypeArguments().forEach(this::written);
    }
  }

  private void reachType(JavaClass type) {
    JavaClass base = type.getBaseComponentType();
    if (!classes.contain(base.getName()) || !types.add(base)) {
      return;
    }
    base.getStaticInitializer().ifPresent(this::reach);
    base.getRawSuperclass().ifPresent(this::reachType);
    base.getRawInterfaces().forEach(this::reachType);
    base.getAnnotations().forEach(annotation -> reachType(annotation.getRawType()));
    // An attribute of an annotation is set wherever the annotation stands, and read by reflection.
    if (base.isAnnotation()) {
      base.getMethods().forEach(this::reach);
    }
  }

  // A record a class literal names is made by reflection, as a row of a query or a read body.
  private void literal(JavaClass type) {
    reachType(type);
    if (type.isRecord()) {
      type.getConstructors().forEach(this::reach);
    }
  }

  // A method that overrides one of a type outside the walk, or one the walk reached, is used.
  private boolean overrides(JavaClass type, JavaMethod method) {
    return Stream.concat(type.getAllRawSuperclasses().stream(), type.getAllRawInterfaces().stream())
        .flatMap(above -> overrideIn(above, method).stream())
        .anyMatch(above -> !classes.contain(above.getOwner().getName()) || members.contains(above));
  }

  private static Optional<JavaMethod> overrideIn(JavaClass type, JavaMethod method) {
    String[] parameters =
        method.getRawParameterTypes().stream().map(JavaClass::getName).toArray(String[]::new);
    return type.tryGetMethod(method.getName(), parameters);
  }

  private void visit(JavaCodeUnit unit) {
    for (JavaAccess<?> access : unit.getAccessesFromSelf()) {
      // A call of an inherited method names the class it calls through as well.
      reachType(access.getTargetOwner());
      boolean written =
          access instanceof JavaFieldAccess field
              && field.getAccessType() == JavaFieldAccess.AccessType.SET;
      if (!written) {
        access.getTarget().resolveMember().ifPresent(this::reach);
      }
    }
    unit.getReferencedClassObjects().forEach(literal -> literal(literal.getRawType()));
    unit.getInstanceofChecks().forEach(check -> reachType(check.getRawType()));
    unit.getRawParameterTypes().forEach(this::reachType);
    reachType(unit.getRawReturnType());
    unit.getThrowsClause().getTypes().forEach(this::reachType);
    unit.getAnnotations().stream().map(JavaAnnotation::getRawType).forEach(this::reachType);
    for (TryCatchBlock block : unit.getTryCatchBlocks()) {
      block.getCaughtThrowables().forEach(this::reachType);
    }
  }

  // No source holds a synthetic class; an anonymous or local class is reported as its maker.
  private static boolean reportable(JavaClass type) {
    return !type.getModifiers().contains(JavaModifier.SYNTHETIC)
        && !type.isAnonymousClass()
        && !type.isLocalClass();
  }

  // A constructor without parameters stops nothing, and an enum always has its two methods.
  private static boolean reportable(JavaCodeUnit unit) {
    boolean bare = unit instanceof JavaConstructor && unit.getRawParameterTypes().isEmpty();
    boolean listed =
        unit.getOwner().isEnum() && Set.of("values", "valueOf").contains(unit.getName());
    return !unit.getModifiers().contains(JavaModifier.SYNTHETIC) && !bare && !listed;
  }

  private static String kindOf(JavaCodeUnit unit) {
    return unit instanceof JavaConstructor ? "constructor" : "method";
  }

  private boolean unusedField(JavaField field, String sources) {
    if (readUnseen(field)) {
      return false;
    }
    // A final field of a primitive or a string may be a constant, whose reads the compiler copies.
    // ponytail: two mentions of the name count as a read, comments too; parsing lifts it.
    boolean constant =
        field.getModifiers().contains(JavaModifier.FINAL)
            && (field.getRawType().isPrimitive()
                || field.getRawType().isEquivalentTo(String.class));
    boolean listed = field.getOwner().isEnum() && field.getRawType().equals(field.getOwner());
    if (constant || listed) {
      return Pattern.compile("\\b" + field.getName() + "\\b").matcher(sources).results().count()
          < 2;
    }
    return !members.contains(field);
  }

  private static boolean readUnseen(JavaField field) {
    // The accessor of a record speaks for its field, which equals and hashCode read unseen.
    boolean component =
        field.getOwner().isRecord() && !field.getModifiers().contains(JavaModifier.STATIC);
    // The serialization of the JDK reads the version of a serializable class, unseen.
    boolean version =
        field.getName().equals("serialVersionUID")
            && field.getOwner().isAssignableTo(Serializable.class);
    return field.getModifiers().contains(JavaModifier.SYNTHETIC) || component || version;
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.deadcode;

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClasses;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaMember;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter;
import dev.metis.tools.Context;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.function.Predicate;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** Walks each project from the listed entry points and its tests from themselves. */
public final class Deadcode {

  private static final String USAGE = "usage: deadcode <file of entry points> <project> ...";
  // The tests of both projects share the sources of this folder.
  private static final String SHARED_TESTS = "test-support/java";
  private static final Pattern ENTRY = Pattern.compile("([\\w.$]+): \\S.*");

  private Deadcode() {}

  /** One line of the list: a class, or a class and a member; its reason is only checked. */
  private record Entry(int line, String pattern) {

    boolean names(JavaMember member) {
      String owner = member.getOwner().getName();
      return pattern.equals(owner) || pattern.equals(owner + "." + member.getName());
    }
  }

  /** Walks each project and prints what nothing reaches. */
  public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    PrintStream out = context.out();
    if (args.size() < 2) {
      out.println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    Path root = context.root();
    String list = args.getFirst();
    List<String> problems = new ArrayList<>();
    List<Entry> entries = entriesOf(root.resolve(list), list, problems);
    Set<Entry> used = new HashSet<>();
    Predicate<JavaMember> listed =
        member -> {
          List<Entry> naming = entries.stream().filter(entry -> entry.names(member)).toList();
          used.addAll(naming);
          return !naming.isEmpty();
        };
    int walked = 0;
    for (String project : args.subList(1, args.size())) {
      JavaClasses main = classesOf(List.of(root.resolve(project + "/build/classes/java/main")));
      // Every source set but main holds tests, which walk together: a helper may serve them all.
      JavaClasses tests = classesOf(testSets(root.resolve(project + "/build/classes/java")));
      String mainSources = sourcesOf(root.resolve(project + "/src/main/java"));
      StringBuilder testSources = new StringBuilder(sourcesOf(root.resolve(SHARED_TESTS)));
      for (Path set : testSets(root.resolve(project + "/src"))) {
        testSources.append(sourcesOf(set.resolve("java")));
      }
      Walk production = new Walk(main).from(listed.or(Walk.SPRING));
      Walk testing = new Walk(tests).from(Walk.TESTS.or(listed).or(Walk.SPRING));
      walked += production.reached() + testing.reached();
      for (String line : production.unused(mainSources)) {
        problems.add(project + ": " + line + " is never used");
      }
      for (String line : testing.unused(testSources.toString())) {
        problems.add(project + " tests: " + line + " is never used");
      }
    }
    entries.stream()
        .filter(entry -> !used.contains(entry))
        .forEach(
            entry ->
                problems.add(list + ":" + entry.line() + ": names nothing: " + entry.pattern()));
    problems.forEach(out::println);
    out.println(
        problems.isEmpty()
            ? "deadcode: clean (" + walked + " classes reached)"
            : "deadcode: " + problems.size() + " problems");
    return problems.isEmpty() ? 0 : 1;
  }

  private static List<Entry> entriesOf(Path file, String list, List<String> problems)
      throws IOException {
    List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(file);
    List<Entry> entries = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int at = 0; at < lines.size(); at++) {
      String line = lines.get(at).strip();
      Matcher entry = ENTRY.matcher(line);
      if (entry.matches()) {
        entries.add(new Entry(at + 1, entry.group(1)));
      } else if (!line.isEmpty() && !line.startsWith("#")) {
        problems.add(list + ":" + (at + 1) + ": no-reason: " + line);
      }
    }
    return entries;
  }

  // A folder that does not exist holds no class.
  private static JavaClasses classesOf(List<Path> folders) {
    return new ClassFileImporter().importPaths(folders);
  }

  // The folders of the source sets of a project but main, which hold its tests.
  private static List<Path> testSets(Path folder) throws IOException {
    if (!Files.isDirectory(folder)) {
      return List.of();
    }
    try (Stream<Path> sets = Files.list(folder)) {
      return sets.filter(set -> !set.getFileName().toString().equals("main")).sorted().toList();
    }
  }

  private static String sourcesOf(Path folder) throws IOException {
    if (!Files.isDirectory(folder)) {
      return "";
    }
    StringBuilder text = new StringBuilder();
    try (Stream<Path> files = Files.walk(folder)) {
      for (Path file : files.filter(path -> path.toString().endsWith(".java")).toList()) {
        text.append(Files.readString(file)).append('\n');
      }
    }
    return text.toString();
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.language;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

// ponytail: it reads tokens, so a Kotlin template holding a quote misleads it; a parser lifts it.
/** The comments of a file, line by line, and the code of a Java file without them. */
public final class Comments {

  /** How a kind of file writes a comment. */
  enum Kind {
    SLASH,
    SQL,
    XML,
    MARKDOWN,
    HASH
  }

  // In a Java or Kotlin file a string or a text block may hold what opens a comment elsewhere.
  private static final Pattern SLASH_TOKEN =
      Pattern.compile("//|/\\*|\"\"\"|\"(?:\\\\.|[^\\\\\"])*\"|'(?:\\\\.|[^\\\\'])*'");
  // In SQL a string doubles its quote to hold one, and a quoted name may hold what opens a comment.
  private static final Pattern SQL_TOKEN =
      Pattern.compile("--|/\\*|'(?:[^']|'')*'|\"(?:[^\"]|\"\")*\"");
  private static final Pattern XML_TOKEN = Pattern.compile("<!--");
  private static final Pattern HASH = Pattern.compile("(^|\\s)#");
  // The title of a test is prose a reader sees beside the comments, so their rules read it too.
  private static final Pattern TITLE =
      Pattern.compile("@DisplayName\\(\\s*\"((?:\\\\.|[^\"\\\\])*)\"");

  private Comments() {}

  /** The kind of a file, by its name. */
  static Kind kindOf(String path) {
    if (path.endsWith(".java") || path.endsWith(".kts")) {
      return Kind.SLASH;
    }
    if (path.endsWith(".sql")) {
      return Kind.SQL;
    }
    if (path.endsWith(".xml")) {
      return Kind.XML;
    }
    return path.endsWith(".md") ? Kind.MARKDOWN : Kind.HASH;
  }

  /** The texts of the comments of each line; Markdown is prose, so a whole line counts. */
  static List<List<String>> of(String path, List<String> lines) {
    Kind kind = kindOf(path);
    Reader reader =
        new Reader(
            switch (kind) {
              case XML -> XML_TOKEN;
              case SQL -> SQL_TOKEN;
              default -> SLASH_TOKEN;
            });
    List<List<String>> comments = new ArrayList<>();
    for (String line : lines) {
      comments.add(
          switch (kind) {
            case MARKDOWN -> List.of(line);
            case HASH -> hashed(line);
            case SLASH, SQL, XML -> reader.read(line).comments();
          });
    }
    if (path.endsWith(".java")) {
      String text = String.join("\n", lines);
      for (Matcher title = TITLE.matcher(text); title.find(); ) {
        long line = text.substring(0, title.start(1)).chars().filter(at -> at == '\n').count();
        comments.get((int) line).add(title.group(1));
      }
    }
    return comments;
  }

  /** The code of each line of a Java file: what is left without its comments and strings. */
  public static List<String> javaCode(List<String> lines) {
    Reader reader = new Reader(SLASH_TOKEN);
    List<String> code = new ArrayList<>();
    for (String line : lines) {
      code.add(reader.read(line).code());
    }
    return code;
  }

  private static List<String> hashed(String line) {
    Matcher hash = HASH.matcher(line);
    return hash.find() ? List.of(line.substring(hash.start())) : List.of();
  }

  /** The comments of one line, and the code around them, its strings left out. */
  private record Line(List<String> comments, String code) {}

  /** Reads a file one line at a time, carrying a block comment or a text block it left open. */
  private static final class Reader {

    private final Pattern tokens;
    private String closer = "";

    private Reader(Pattern tokens) {
      this.tokens = tokens;
    }

    private Line read(String line) {
      List<String> texts = new ArrayList<>();
      StringBuilder code = new StringBuilder();
      int at = 0;
      while (at >= 0) {
        at = closer.isEmpty() ? token(line, at, texts, code) : span(line, at, texts);
      }
      return new Line(texts, code.toString());
    }

    // From at to the closer of the open span, or to the end of the line; only a comment is kept.
    private int span(String line, int at, List<String> texts) {
      int end = line.indexOf(closer, at);
      if (!closer.equals("\"\"\"")) {
        texts.add(line.substring(at, end < 0 ? line.length() : end));
      }
      if (end < 0) {
        return -1;
      }
      int next = end + closer.length();
      closer = "";
      return next;
    }

    // The next token from at: a line comment ends the line, a block or a text block opens a span.
    private int token(String line, int at, List<String> texts, StringBuilder code) {
      Matcher token = tokens.matcher(line);
      if (!token.find(at)) {
        code.append(line, at, line.length());
        return -1;
      }
      code.append(line, at, token.start());
      switch (token.group()) {
        case "//", "--" -> {
          texts.add(line.substring(token.end()));
          return -1;
        }
        case "/*" -> closer = "*/";
        case "<!--" -> closer = "-->";
        case "\"\"\"" -> closer = "\"\"\"";
        default -> {
          // A string or a character, stepped over.
        }
      }
      return token.end();
    }
  }
}
```

`tools/build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("metis.java-conventions")
    application
}

application {
    mainClass = "dev.metis.tools.Main"
}

dependencies {
    implementation(libs.archunit)
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-core")
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind")
}

// A command of the tool, run from the repository root, for a check of the root build to depend on.
fun tool(name: String, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<JavaExec>(name) {
        classpath = sourceSets.main.get().runtimeClasspath
        mainClass = application.mainClass
        workingDir = rootDir
        args(*arguments)
    }

tool("language", "language")
tool("marks", "marks")
// The walk resolves the types the classes of both projects extend, so it runs on their classpaths.
evaluationDependsOn(":core")
tool("deadcode", "deadcode", "config/entry-points.txt", "core", "tools").configure {
    val core = project(":core").the<SourceSetContainer>()
    classpath += core["test"].runtimeClasspath + core["integrationTest"].runtimeClasspath +
        sourceSets.test.get().runtimeClasspath
    dependsOn(":core:testClasses", ":core:integrationTestClasses", tasks.testClasses)
}
// The judges of the test tasks, which run after the tests even when a test failed.
tool("judgeArchitecture", "tests", "architecture", "core/build/test-results/architectureTest", "tools/build/test-results/architectureTest")
    .configure { mustRunAfter(":core:architectureTest", tasks.named("architectureTest")) }
tool("judgeDeadcode", "tests", "deadcode", "core/build/test-results/deadcodeTest")
    .configure { mustRunAfter(":core:deadcodeTest") }
tool(
    "judgeCoverage", "coverage", "core/build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml",
    "tools/build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml",
).configure { mustRunAfter(":core:jacocoTestReport", tasks.jacocoTestReport) }
// What PIT mutates: the classes of -Pmutate, else the classes changed since MUTATION_BASE, else all.
tool("mutationScope", "mutation-scope").configure {
    val given = providers.gradleProperty("mutate").map { listOf("--given", it) }
    val base = providers.environmentVariable("MUTATION_BASE").filter { it.isNotBlank() }.map { listOf("--base", it) }
    argumentProviders.add(CommandLineArgumentProvider { given.orElse(base).getOrElse(listOf()) + listOf("core", "tools") })
}
tool("judgeMutation", "mutation", "core", "tools").configure { mustRunAfter(":core:pitest", tasks.pitest) }
tool("imageRun", "image", "metis-core:check").configure { dependsOn(":imageBuild") }
tool("judgeTooling", "tests", "tooling", "tools/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(tasks.test) }
tool("judgeUnit", "tests", "unit", "core/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(":core:test") }
tool("judgeIntegration", "tests", "integration", "core/build/test-results/integrationTest")
    .configure { mustRunAfter(":core:integrationTest") }

// ./verify and ./canary start the tool with the Java and the classpath this task writes, and the tool
// learns from it the check tasks Gradle has in every project, however a build file declares them.
val launcher = tasks.register("launcher") {
    val executable = javaToolchains.launcherFor(java.toolchain).map { it.executablePath.asFile.path }
    val classpath = sourceSets.main.map { it.runtimeClasspath }
    val checks = rootProject.allprojects.flatMap { project ->
        val prefix = if (project == rootProject) "" else project.path + ":"
        project.tasks.names.filter { it.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) }.map { prefix + it }
    }
    val folder = layout.buildDirectory.dir("launcher")
    inputs.files(classpath)
    inputs.property("java", executable)
    inputs.property("checks", checks)
    outputs.dir(folder)
    doLast {
        folder.get().file("java").asFile.writeText(executable.get() + "\n")
        folder.get().file("args").asFile.writeText("-cp\n\"" + classpath.get().asPath + "\"\n")
        folder.get().file("checks").asFile.writeText(checks.joinToString("") { "$it\n" })
    }
}

// The tests of the counter-tests read the list of checks the launcher writes.
tasks.named("testClasses") { dependsOn(launcher) }
```
