`tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/image/ImageCheck.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.tools.image;

import dev.metis.tools.Context;
import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.Processes;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.UUID;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/** Runs the image from the compose file of the stack, as a deployment does, and records it. */
public final class ImageCheck {

  // A project of its own on a free port, so a local stack that runs is left alone.
  private static final String PROJECT = "metis-check";
  private static final List<String> COMPOSE =
      List.of("docker", "compose", "--project-name", PROJECT, "--file", "stack/compose.yaml");
  private static final String CONTAINER = PROJECT + "-core-1";
  // The stack reads every password from the environment, and each run makes its own.
  private static final List<String> PASSWORDS =
      List.of("METIS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD", "METIS_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD", "METIS_APP_PASSWORD");
  private static final String PERSON_PASSWORD = "METIS_PERSON_PASSWORD";
  private static final String LOCKDOWN =
      "{{.HostConfig.ReadonlyRootfs}}|{{json .HostConfig.CapDrop}}|{{json .HostConfig.SecurityOpt}}"
          + "|{{.HostConfig.Memory}}|{{.HostConfig.NanoCpus}}|{{json .HostConfig.Tmpfs}}"
          + "|{{.Config.StopTimeout}}|{{json .HostConfig.CapAdd}}|{{.HostConfig.Privileged}}"
          + "|{{json .Mounts}}";
  // A read-only root with one temporary folder, no capability, no new privilege, 2 GB, one
  // processor, 30 seconds of grace, nothing added, no privileged mode and no mount, as compose
  // must say.
  private static final String LOCKED =
      "true|[\"ALL\"]|[\"no-new-privileges:true\"]|2147483648|1000000000|{\"/tmp\":\"\"}|30"
          + "|null|false|[]";
  private static final String UP = "{\"status\":\"UP\"}";
  // What Flyway says of a database without a migration of the image, the reason to refuse it.
  private static final String BEHIND = "Detected resolved migration not applied to database";
  private static final int READY_SECONDS = 60;
  // Compose waits this long for what a service depends on, so a job that never ends turns red.
  private static final int START_SECONDS = 120;
  private static final int GRACE_SECONDS = 30;
  // The running core itself: its user, its capabilities, its root mount and any build tool.
  private static final String PROBE =
      "id -u || exit 1; grep -E '^Cap(Eff|Bnd):' /proc/1/status || exit 1; grep ' / ' /proc/mounts"
          + " || exit 1; for tool in javac jar gradle mvn; do command -v \"$tool\"; done; exit 0";
  private static final Pattern NO_CAPABILITY = Pattern.compile("Cap(Eff|Bnd):\\s+0+");
  private static final Pattern ROOT_MOUNT = Pattern.compile("\\S+ / \\S+ (\\S+) .*");
  private final Context context;
  private final String image;
  private final List<String> problems = new ArrayList<>();
  private final Map<String, String> passwords = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  private final String person = UUID.randomUUID().toString();

  private ImageCheck(Context context, String image) {
    this.context = context;
    this.image = image;
    PASSWORDS.forEach(name -> passwords.put(name, UUID.randomUUID().toString()));
    passwords.put(PERSON_PASSWORD, person);
  }

  /** Checks the image the argument names and leaves its measures as facts. */
  public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    PrintStream out = context.out();
    if (args.size() != 1) {
      out.println("usage: image <image>");
      return 2;
    }
    ImageCheck check = new ImageCheck(context, args.getFirst());
    Processes.Result size = check.docker("image", "inspect", "--format", "{{.Size}}", check.image);
    if (size.status() != 0) {
      out.println("image: no image " + check.image + ": " + size.output().strip());
      return 1;
    }
    String facts =
        String.format(
                Locale.ROOT, "image content %.1f MB, ", Long.parseLong(size.output().strip()) / 1e6)
            + check.run();
    check.problems.forEach(problem -> out.println("image: " + problem));
    out.println("image: " + facts);
    Facts.write(context.root(), "image", facts);
    return check.problems.isEmpty() ? 0 : 1;
  }

  // Runs the stack with the image and gives the facts after the size; each run starts from
  // nothing, the volumes of the project included.
  private String run() throws IOException {
    compose("down", "--volumes");
    try {
      refused();
      Processes.Result started =
          compose("up", "--detach", "--no-build", "--wait-timeout", String.valueOf(START_SECONDS));
      if (started.status() != 0) {
        problems.add("the stack did not start: " + started.output().strip());
        problems.addAll(last(compose("logs", "--no-color", "migrate").output()));
        return "never started";
      }
      return running();
    } finally {
      compose("down", "--volumes");
    }
  }

  // The API alone, on a database no migration job ran on, must refuse to start, for that reason.
  private void refused() {
    compose(
        "up",
        "--detach",
        "--no-build",
        "--no-deps",
        "--wait",
        "--wait-timeout",
        String.valueOf(START_SECONDS),
        "postgres");
    compose("up", "--detach", "--no-build", "--no-deps", "core");
    boolean ready = probe("readiness", READY_SECONDS).output().strip().equals(UP);
    // The probe ends with the process of a refused start, whose container may still be stopping.
    docker("stop", "--timeout", String.valueOf(GRACE_SECONDS), CONTAINER);
    String state =
        docker("inspect", "--format", "{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}}", CONTAINER)
            .output()
            .strip();
    String log = compose("logs", "--no-color", "core").output();
    if (ready || !state.matches("exited [1-9]\\d*") || !log.contains(BEHIND)) {
      problems.add("the API did not refuse a database no migration job ran on: " + state);
      problems.addAll(last(log));
    }
  }

  // The last lines of a log, which say why a container stopped or never ended.
  private static List<String> last(String log) {
    List<String> lines = log.strip().lines().toList();
    return lines.subList(Math.max(0, lines.size() - 20), lines.size());
  }

  private String running() throws IOException {
    String locked = docker("inspect", "--format", LOCKDOWN, CONTAINER).output().strip();
    if (!locked.equals(LOCKED)) {
      problems.add("the stack does not run the core locked down: " + locked);
    }
    connectsAsTheApi();
    long start = context.nanos().getAsLong();
    Processes.Result ready = probe("readiness", READY_SECONDS);
    double seconds = (context.nanos().getAsLong() - start) / 1e9;
    if (ready.status() != 0 || !ready.output().strip().equals(UP)) {
      problems.add("the container was never ready");
      compose("logs", "--no-color", "--tail", "20").output().strip().lines().forEach(problems::add);
      return "never ready";
    }
    if (seconds > READY_SECONDS) {
      problems.add(
          String.format(Locale.ROOT, "ready after %.1f s, past %d s", seconds, READY_SECONDS));
    }
    inside();
    problems.addAll(new ShellRead(context, PROJECT).problems(person));
    Processes.Result live = probe("liveness", 0);
    if (!live.output().strip().equals(UP)) {
      problems.add("liveness answered " + live.output().strip());
    }
    String memory =
        docker("stats", "--no-stream", "--format", "{{.MemUsage}}", CONTAINER).output().strip();
    stop();
    return String.format(
        Locale.ROOT, "ready in %.1f s, memory %s", seconds, memory.replaceAll(" /.*", ""));
  }

  // The API connects as its own role and holds nothing that could switch a policy off.
  private void connectsAsTheApi() {
    String environment = docker("inspect", "--format", "{{json .Config.Env}}", CONTAINER).output();
    if (!environment.contains("\"SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME=metis_app\"")) {
      problems.add("the core does not connect as metis_app");
    }
    if (environment.contains("metis_migrator")
        || environment.contains(Objects.requireNonNull(passwords.get("METIS_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD")))
        || environment.contains(Objects.requireNonNull(passwords.get("METIS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD")))) {
      problems.add(
          "the core holds the role or a password of the owner of the tables or of the superuser");
    }
  }

  // Whatever the image or the compose file say, the running core is not the user 0, holds no
  // capability, has a read-only root and no build tool; a probe that fails proves none of it.
  private void inside() {
    Processes.Result probe =
        context
            .quiet()
            .apply(context.root(), List.of("docker", "exec", CONTAINER, "sh", "-c", PROBE));
    List<String> lines = probe.output().strip().lines().toList();
    Matcher mount = ROOT_MOUNT.matcher(lines.size() > 3 ? lines.get(3) : "");
    if (probe.status() != 0 || !lines.getFirst().matches("\\d+") || !mount.matches()) {
      problems.add(
          "cannot read the user and the capabilities of the core: " + probe.output().strip());
      return;
    }
    if (lines.getFirst().equals("0")) {
      problems.add("the core runs as root");
    }
    if (!NO_CAPABILITY.matcher(lines.get(1)).matches()
        || !NO_CAPABILITY.matcher(lines.get(2)).matches()) {
      problems.add(
          "the core runs with a capability: "
              + (lines.get(1) + ", " + lines.get(2)).replaceAll("\\s+", " "));
    }
    // The first option of the mount says how it is mounted; the others name the layers.
    String mode = mount.group(1).replaceFirst(",.*", "");
    if (!mode.equals("ro")) {
      problems.add("the root file system of the core is writable: " + mode);
    }
    if (lines.size() > 4) {
      problems.add(
          "the image holds a build tool: " + String.join(" ", lines.subList(4, lines.size())));
    }
  }

  // The JVM runs as the first process, so the signal reaches it and it exits with 128 and 15.
  private void stop() {
    long start = context.nanos().getAsLong();
    compose("stop", "core");
    double seconds = (context.nanos().getAsLong() - start) / 1e9;
    String exit = docker("inspect", "--format", "{{.State.ExitCode}}", CONTAINER).output().strip();
    if (!exit.equals("143") || seconds >= GRACE_SECONDS) {
      problems.add(
          String.format(
              Locale.ROOT,
              "a stop signal did not end the JVM inside the grace period: exit %s after %.1f s",
              exit,
              seconds));
    }
  }

  // curl waits between its tries inside the container, so the check keeps no clock of its own.
  // ponytail: the time to ready is known to the second; a shorter delay between tries lifts it.
  private Processes.Result probe(String probe, int tries) {
    return docker(
        "exec",
        CONTAINER,
        "curl",
        "--fail",
        "--silent",
        "--max-time",
        "2",
        "--retry",
        String.valueOf(tries),
        "--retry-delay",
        "1",
        "--retry-all-errors",
        "http://localhost:8080/actuator/health/" + probe);
  }

  // The stack runs the image under test, on a free port, in a time zone that is not UTC.
  private Processes.Result compose(String... args) {
    List<String> command =
        new ArrayList<>(
            List.of(
                "env", "METIS_IMAGE=" + image, "METIS_PORT=", "METIS_TIME_ZONE=Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh"));
    passwords.forEach((name, value) -> command.add(name + "=" + value));
    command.addAll(COMPOSE);
    command.addAll(List.of(args));
    return context.run().apply(context.root(), command);
  }

  private Processes.Result docker(String... args) {
    List<String> command = new ArrayList<>(List.of("docker"));
    command.addAll(List.of(args));
    return context.run().apply(context.root(), command);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;

/**
 * The counter-tests of the image check: a line added to the Dockerfile wins, or a change of stack.
 */
final class ImageCanaries {

  private static final String DOCKERFILE = "core/Dockerfile";

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          Canary.of("image-root", "image", "the core runs as root")
              .appending(DOCKERFILE, "USER root\n"),
          // A shell running more than the JVM holds the stop signal back from it until grace ends.
          Canary.of("image-shell-entrypoint", "image", "inside the grace period")
              .appending(DOCKERFILE, "ENTRYPOINT java -jar core.jar && echo stopped\n"),
          Canary.of("image-root-write", "image", "Read-only file system")
              .appending(
                  DOCKERFILE,
                  "ENTRYPOINT [\"sh\", \"-c\", \"touch /started && exec java -jar core.jar\"]\n"),
          // The root user again, which the linter of the Dockerfile names on its own.
          Canary.of("image-hadolint", "image", "DL3002").appending(DOCKERFILE, "USER root\n"),
          // A library with a known vulnerability in the image, which only the scan of the image
          // sees.
          Canary.of("image-scan", "image", "CVE-2021-44228")
              .appending(
                  DOCKERFILE,
                  "ADD https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/apache/logging/log4j/log4j-core/2.14.1/"
                      + "log4j-core-2.14.1.jar /app/lib/\n"),
          // A writable root in the compose file, which the check reads back from the container.
          Canary.of("image-compose-writable", "image", "does not run the core locked down")
              .replacing("stack/compose.yaml", "    read_only: true\n", ""),
          // The root user in the compose file, which the image alone does not show.
          Canary.of("image-compose-root", "image", "the core runs as root")
              .replacing(
                  "stack/compose.yaml",
                  "    read_only: true\n",
                  "    user: \"0\"\n    read_only: true\n"),
          // A core that trusts another issuer, so the token of the stack's Keycloak is refused.
          Canary.of("image-wrong-issuer", "image", "the shell answered 401")
              .replacing(
                  "stack/compose.yaml",
                  "METIS_SECURITY_ISSUER: http://keycloak:8080/realms/metis",
                  "METIS_SECURITY_ISSUER: http://keycloak:8080/realms/other"),
          // An API that starts without checking the migrations of its database.
          Canary.of(
                  "image-unchecked-database",
                  "image",
                  "the API did not refuse a database no migration job ran on")
              .replacing(
                  "stack/compose.yaml",
                  "METIS_SECURITY_ISSUER: http://keycloak:8080/realms/metis",
                  "METIS_SECURITY_ISSUER: http://keycloak:8080/realms/metis\n"
                      + "      SPRING_FLYWAY_ENABLED: \"false\""),
          // The password of the owner of the tables given to the API, which then holds that role.
          Canary.of("image-owner-password", "image", "the core holds")
              .replacing(
                  "stack/compose.yaml",
                  "      METIS_SECURITY_ISSUER:",
                  "      SPRING_FLYWAY_PASSWORD: ${METIS_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD:?x}\n"
                      + "      METIS_SECURITY_ISSUER:"),
          // A capability the compose file adds back, which the running core then holds.
          Canary.of("image-compose-capability", "image", "the core runs with a capability")
              .replacing(
                  "stack/compose.yaml",
                  "    cap_drop:\n      - ALL\n",
                  "    cap_add:\n      - NET_RAW\n    cap_drop:\n      - ALL\n"));

  private ImageCanaries() {}
}
```

Add the files the list above names, the generated ones included, to the ledger of the run. Never run git add, git commit or git push: the owner commits.

### Task 8: The modules and the rules inside them

Spring Modulith verifies the two modules: `platform` declares no dependency and names its interfaces `web` and `security`; `workspace` may use those two alone, and no module reaches a hidden package of another. ArchUnit adds the rules inside a module: a controller calls a use case and a use case the rules and the repositories, never back up; a rule of `domain` uses nothing of Spring nor of the other layers; a transaction starts in a use case alone; no module reads the person of a request from a static holder; no code makes a bean with `new`; a controller calls no rule of `domain`, whose types it may still name; a transaction starts in a use case alone, by annotation or by a transaction API. Only a repository and the tenant hook reach the database; the text of every statement is a string constant loaded right before `JdbcClient.sql`, which a rule reads from the class files with the JDK's own `java.lang.classfile`, so SQL handed in as a parameter fails too; a repository calls nothing but the three types of `JdbcClient` today's repositories call, read with `javap`, so it builds no SQL and hides no decision in a library call; and a repository holds no decision, a cyclomatic complexity of 1, which the lint check measures. The core compiles with `-XDstringConcat=inline`, so a join of strings is a call of `StringBuilder`, which the rule of the calls refuses.

```kotlin
import java.time.Duration

plugins {
    id("metis.java-conventions")
    alias(libs.plugins.spring.boot)
    alias(libs.plugins.license.report)
}

// What the tests of both kinds share, such as the issuer of their tokens.
val shared = layout.projectDirectory.dir("src/testShared/java")
sourceSets.test {
    java.srcDir(shared)
}

// The tests on a real PostgreSQL and a real Keycloak, apart from the tests that need no container.
val integrationTest = sourceSets.create("integrationTest") {
    java.srcDir(shared)
    java.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/java"))
    // The architecture rules run with the unit tests alone, and need ArchUnit, which these lack.
    java.exclude("**/ArchitectureRules.java")
    resources.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/resources"))
    compileClasspath += sourceSets.main.get().output
    runtimeClasspath += sourceSets.main.get().output
}

// As the unit tests do, so the versions and the libraries of the core hold for them too.
configurations[integrationTest.implementationConfigurationName].extendsFrom(configurations.implementation.get())
configurations[integrationTest.runtimeOnlyConfigurationName].extendsFrom(configurations.runtimeOnly.get())

dependencies {
    implementation(platform(libs.spring.modulith.bom))
    implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc")
    implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-jdbc")
    implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-flyway")
    implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-security-oauth2-resource-server")
    implementation("org.slf4j:slf4j-api")
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind")
    compileOnly("org.springframework.modulith:spring-modulith-api")
    runtimeOnly("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-actuator")
    runtimeOnly("org.flywaydb:flyway-database-postgresql")
    runtimeOnly("org.postgresql:postgresql")
    testImplementation(libs.archunit)
    testImplementation("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-params")
    testImplementation("org.mockito:mockito-core")
    testImplementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-security-test")
    testImplementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test")
    testImplementation("org.springframework.modulith:spring-modulith-core")
    "integrationTestImplementation"(platform(libs.junit.bom))
    "integrationTestImplementation"("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api")
    "integrationTestImplementation"("org.assertj:assertj-core")
    "integrationTestImplementation"("org.awaitility:awaitility")
    "integrationTestImplementation"("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-params")
    "integrationTestImplementation"("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test")
    "integrationTestImplementation"("org.testcontainers:testcontainers")
    "integrationTestImplementation"("org.testcontainers:testcontainers-postgresql")
    "integrationTestImplementation"("org.yaml:snakeyaml")
    "integrationTestImplementation"(libs.datasource.proxy)
    "integrationTestCompileOnly"("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    "integrationTestCompileOnly"("org.springframework.modulith:spring-modulith-api")
    "integrationTestRuntimeOnly"("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-engine")
    "integrationTestRuntimeOnly"("org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher")
}

// Mockito joins each test JVM as an agent from the start, since the JDK will refuse a late one.
val mockitoAgent = configurations.create("mockitoAgent")
dependencies {
    mockitoAgent(platform(libs.spring.boot.bom))
    mockitoAgent("org.mockito:mockito-core") { isTransitive = false }
}
val agent = mockitoAgent.elements.map { "-javaagent:" + it.single().asFile.path }
tasks.withType<Test>().configureEach { jvmArgumentProviders.add(CommandLineArgumentProvider { listOf(agent.get()) }) }
pitest {
    jvmArgs.add(agent)
}

// A join of strings compiles to calls of StringBuilder, which the architecture check can see.
tasks.compileJava {
    options.compilerArgs.add("-XDstringConcat=inline")
}

val integrationTestTask = tasks.register<Test>("integrationTest") {
    description = "Runs the tests on a real PostgreSQL and a real Keycloak."
    testClassesDirs = integrationTest.output.classesDirs
    classpath = integrationTest.runtimeClasspath
    // One JVM, so the containers and the contexts of Spring start once for every class.
    maxParallelForks = 1
    // The tests read the stack's own files, so the stack and the tests share one source.
    workingDir = rootDir
    // Those files are inputs, so a changed stack runs the tests again and no cached result stands in.
    inputs.dir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("stack")).withPathSensitivity(PathSensitivity.RELATIVE)
    // A test that would wait for ever fails the check after this instead of holding it.
    timeout = Duration.ofMinutes(20)
}

// Coverage counts the lines both test tasks run, since only a database runs a repository.
tasks.jacocoTestReport {
    dependsOn(integrationTestTask)
    executionData(tasks.test.get(), integrationTestTask.get())
}

// A repository holds no decision, only SQL and the one call that runs it, which a database tests.
tasks.register<Checkstyle>("checkstyleData") {
    description = "No method of a repository makes a decision."
    source = fileTree("src/main/java") { include("**/internal/data/**/*.java") }
    classpath = files()
    checkstyleClasspath = configurations.checkstyle.get()
    configFile = rootProject.file("config/checkstyle/data.xml")
    reports {
        xml.required = false
        html.required = false
    }
}
```

```kotlin
plugins {

dependencyLocking {

spotless {
    java {
        target("core/src/**/*.java", "tools/src/**/*.java", "test-support/**/*.java")

        removeUnusedImports()
    }
    format("misc") {
        target(
            "**/*.kts", "**/*.md", "**/*.yml", "**/*.yaml", "**/*.toml", "**/*.properties",
            "**/*.json", "**/*.xml", "**/*.txt", "**/Dockerfile", "**/.gitignore", ".dockerignore",

        trimTrailingWhitespace()
        endWithNewline()
    }

// A scanner that is no Gradle plugin, run as its pinned image in the tree, which it reads only.
fun scanner(name: String, image: Provider<String>, options: List<String>, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<Exec>(name) {
        val tree = rootDir.absolutePath
        commandLine(
            listOf("docker", "run", "--rm", "--volume", "$tree:/work:ro", "--workdir", "/work") +
                options + listOf(image.get()) + arguments,
        )
    }

// Trivy keeps its database in a volume of its own, so a scan downloads it once a day at most.
val trivy = listOf("--volume", "metis-trivy-cache:/root/.cache")

scanner(
    "depsVulnerabilities", libs.versions.image.trivy, trivy,
    "fs", "--scanners", "vuln", "--exit-code", "1", "--quiet",
    "--skip-dirs", "/work/build", "--skip-dirs", "/work/**/build", "--skip-dirs", "/work/.gradle", "/work",
)

// A relative folder, so the paths the allow-list of .gitleaks.toml matches start at the root.
scanner(
    "secretsScan", libs.versions.image.gitleaks, listOf(),
    "dir", ".", "--no-banner", "--redact", "--verbose", "--config", ".gitleaks.toml",
)

// actionlint finds the workflows through .git, which the copy of a canary lacks, so each is named.
val workflows = file(".github/workflows").list().orEmpty().sorted().map { ".github/workflows/$it" }

scanner("workflowLint", libs.versions.image.actionlint, listOf(), "-color", *workflows.toTypedArray())

// The image the image check builds from the sources, with Docker alone, as any platform would.
tasks.register<Exec>("imageBuild") {
    commandLine("docker", "build", "--file", "core/Dockerfile", "--tag", "metis-core:check", ".")
}

tasks.register<Exec>("imageLint") {
    val dockerfile = file("core/Dockerfile")
    commandLine("docker", "run", "--rm", "--interactive", libs.versions.image.hadolint.get(), "hadolint", "-")
    doFirst {
        standardInput = dockerfile.inputStream()
    }
}

// Trivy reads the image from an archive in the tree, so it needs no hand on the Docker daemon.
tasks.register<Exec>("imageSave") {
    dependsOn("imageBuild")
    val archive = layout.buildDirectory.file("image/core.tar")
    doFirst {
        archive.get().asFile.parentFile.mkdirs()
    }
    commandLine("docker", "save", "--output", archive.get().asFile.path, "metis-core:check")
}

scanner(
    "imageScan", libs.versions.image.trivy, trivy,
    "image", "--input", "/work/build/image/core.tar", "--scanners", "vuln", "--exit-code", "1", "--quiet",
).configure { dependsOn("imageSave") }

// The checks of ./verify, which runs them in the order of the list of the tool, Checks.ORDER.

tasks.register("checkFormat") {
    description = "Every source file is formatted."
    dependsOn("spotlessCheck")
}

tasks.register("checkCompile") {
    description = "The code compiles with every warning an error, no bug pattern and no null where none is allowed."
    dependsOn(
        ":core:compileJava", ":core:compileTestJava", ":core:compileIntegrationTestJava",
        ":tools:compileJava", ":tools:compileTestJava",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkLint") {
    description = "No method above a complexity of 10, no file above 300 lines, a reason on every mark."
    dependsOn(
        ":core:checkstyleMain", ":core:checkstyleTest", ":core:checkstyleIntegrationTest",
        ":core:checkstyleData", ":tools:checkstyleMain", ":tools:checkstyleTest", ":tools:marks",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkLanguage") {
    description = "English only, and no comment that cites a plan, a ruling, a task, a date or a line of a file."
    dependsOn(":tools:language")
}

tasks.register("checkArchitecture") {
    description = "The architecture rules of both projects hold."
    dependsOn(":core:architectureTest", ":tools:architectureTest", ":tools:judgeArchitecture")
}

tasks.register("checkDeadcode") {
    description = "Nothing unused: code, test helpers, dependencies and settings."
    dependsOn(
        ":core:projectHealth", ":tools:projectHealth", "bundledDeclared", ":tools:deadcode",
        ":core:deadcodeTest", ":tools:judgeDeadcode",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkTooling") {
    description = "The tests of the tool pass, every check has a counter-test, the workflow passes its linter."
    dependsOn(":tools:test", ":tools:judgeTooling", "workflowLint")
}

tasks.register("checkUnit") {
    description = "The tests of the core that need no container pass, none skipped, as many as the floor."
    dependsOn(":core:test", ":tools:judgeUnit")
}

tasks.register("checkIntegration") {
    description = "The tests on a real PostgreSQL and a real Keycloak pass, none skipped, as many as the floor."
    dependsOn(":core:integrationTest", ":tools:judgeIntegration")
}

tasks.register("checkCoverage") {
    description = "Every line and every branch of the core and the tool runs in a test."
    dependsOn(":core:jacocoTestReport", ":tools:jacocoTestReport", ":tools:judgeCoverage")
}

tasks.register("checkMutation") {

    dependsOn(":core:pitest", ":tools:pitest", ":tools:judgeMutation")

tasks.register("checkDeps") {

    dependsOn("imageLint", "imageBuild", "imageScan", ":tools:imageRun")
}

// A check whose judge did not run would pass on the exit of its tasks alone, so a check that owes
// facts fails without them; ./verify and ./canary clear the facts before each run of a check.
val factFree = setOf("checkFormat", "checkCompile", "checkDeps", "checkSecrets")
tasks.matching { it.name.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) && it.name !in factFree }.configureEach {
    val check = name.removePrefix("check").replaceFirstChar(Char::lowercase)
    val facts = layout.buildDirectory.file("facts/$check.txt")
    doLast {
        if (!facts.get().asFile.exists()) {
            throw GradleException("$name: its judge left no facts in build/facts/$check.txt")
        }
    }
}

// A starter stands for the libraries of it that the code uses, named one by one, which the plugin
// would otherwise ask to declare; a library a bundle names is never reported unused, so
// bundledDeclared refuses a project that declares one of them itself.
val starters =
    mapOf(
        "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc" to listOf(
            "org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-autoconfigure",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-tomcat",

            "org.springframework:spring-context",
            "org.springframework:spring-core",
            "org.springframework:spring-web",
            "org.springframework:spring-webmvc",
        ),
        "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-jdbc" to listOf(
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-transaction",
            "org.springframework:spring-jdbc",
            "org.springframework:spring-tx",
        ),
        "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-flyway" to listOf(
            "org.flywaydb:flyway-core",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-flyway",
        ),
        "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-security-oauth2-resource-server" to listOf(
            "com.nimbusds:nimbus-jose-jwt",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-security",
            "org.springframework.security:spring-security-config",
            "org.springframework.security:spring-security-core",
            "org.springframework.security:spring-security-oauth2-core",
            "org.springframework.security:spring-security-oauth2-jose",
            "org.springframework.security:spring-security-oauth2-resource-server",
            "org.springframework.security:spring-security-web",
        ),
        "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test" to listOf(

            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-test",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-webmvc-test",
            "org.springframework:spring-beans",
            "org.springframework:spring-test",
        ),
        "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-security-test" to listOf(
            "org.springframework.security:spring-security-test",
        ),
    )

configure<com.autonomousapps.DependencyAnalysisExtension> {
    structure {
        starters.forEach { (starter, libraries) ->
            bundle(starter.substringAfter(':')) {
                primary(starter)
                libraries.forEach { includeDependency(it) }
            }
        }
    }
    issues {
        all {
            onAny {
                severity("fail")
            }
        }
    }
}

val bundled = tasks.register("bundledDeclared") {
    description = "No project declares a library that a bundle names."
}

gradle.projectsEvaluated {
    val members = starters.values.flatten().toSet()
    val declared =
        subprojects.flatMap { project ->
            project.configurations.flatMap { configuration ->
                configuration.dependencies
                    .filter { "${it.group}:${it.name}" in members }
                    .map { "${it.group}:${it.name} in ${project.path} ${configuration.name}" }
            }
        }
    bundled.configure {
        doLast {
            if (declared.isNotEmpty()) {
                throw GradleException("a bundle names what a project declares, which it would never report: $declared")
            }
        }
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the lock files and the checksums again**

A configuration in strict mode resolves only against its lock state, and an artifact only against its checksum, so a change of the dependencies writes both again, with every task run for real, since a task restored from the build cache resolves nothing.

```sh
./gradlew --console=plain --max-workers=5 --refresh-dependencies --write-locks --write-verification-metadata sha256 --rerun-tasks help spotlessCheck :core:checkLicense
```

```java
package dev.metis.core;

import static com.tngtech.archunit.base.DescribedPredicate.not;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaCall.Predicates.target;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClass.Predicates.resideInAPackage;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.properties.CanBeAnnotated.Predicates.metaAnnotatedWith;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.properties.HasName.Predicates.nameMatching;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.properties.HasOwner.Predicates.With.owner;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.properties.HasParameterTypes.Predicates.rawParameterTypes;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noMethods;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.library.Architectures.layeredArchitecture;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import com.tngtech.archunit.base.DescribedPredicate;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClass;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClasses;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption;
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses;
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTag;
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.CompositeArchRule;
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.GeneralCodingRules;
import dev.metis.testsupport.ArchitectureRules;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.lang.classfile.ClassFile;
import java.lang.classfile.CodeElement;
import java.lang.classfile.CodeModel;
import java.lang.classfile.Instruction;
import java.lang.classfile.MethodModel;
import java.lang.classfile.instruction.ConstantInstruction;
import java.lang.classfile.instruction.InvokeInstruction;
import java.sql.Connection;
import java.sql.Statement;
import java.time.Clock;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.Set;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcOperations;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.namedparam.NamedParameterJdbcTemplate;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.modulith.core.ApplicationModules;
import org.springframework.security.core.context.SecurityContextHolder;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import org.springframework.transaction.PlatformTransactionManager;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionOperations;
import org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate;
import org.springframework.web.context.request.RequestContextHolder;

@ArchTag("architecture")
@AnalyzeClasses(packages = "dev.metis.core", importOptions = ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class)
class ArchitectureTest {

  // The calls of java.time and of System that read the time or the zone of the machine.
  private static final DescribedPredicate<JavaClass> TIME =
      DescribedPredicate.describe(
          "java.time or java.lang.System",
          type -> type.getPackageName().equals("java.time") || type.isEquivalentTo(System.class));

  // The types that run SQL on a connection of the database.
  private static final DescribedPredicate<JavaClass> JDBC =
      DescribedPredicate.describe(
          "a type that runs SQL",
          type ->
              type.getName().startsWith(JdbcClient.class.getName())
                  || type.isEquivalentTo(JdbcTemplate.class)
                  || type.isEquivalentTo(NamedParameterJdbcTemplate.class)
                  || type.isEquivalentTo(JdbcOperations.class)
                  || type.isEquivalentTo(Connection.class)
                  || type.isAssignableTo(Statement.class));

  // What the repositories call, read from their class files: three types of JdbcClient.
  private static final Set<String> STATEMENT =
      Set.of(
          JdbcClient.class.getName(),
          JdbcClient.StatementSpec.class.getName(),
          JdbcClient.MappedQuerySpec.class.getName());

  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule constructorInjectionOnly =
      GeneralCodingRules.NO_CLASSES_SHOULD_USE_FIELD_INJECTION;

  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule logsGoThroughTheLogger =
      GeneralCodingRules.NO_CLASSES_SHOULD_ACCESS_STANDARD_STREAMS;

  // The clock bean is the only time the core reads, so a profile and a test can fix the date.
  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule noSystemClock =
      noClasses()
          .that()
          .resideOutsideOfPackage("dev.metis.core.platform.time.internal")
          .should()
          .callMethodWhere(
              target(owner(TIME))
                  .and(target(nameMatching("now|currentTimeMillis|system.*")))
                  .and(not(target(rawParameterTypes(Clock.class)))))
          .as("no classes should read the system clock or the system time zone");

  @ArchTest static final ArchRule nullMarked = ArchitectureRules.NULL_MARKED;

  @ArchTest static final ArchRule noLegacyDates = ArchitectureRules.LEGACY_DATES;

  // Each module reaches only the modules and the named interfaces its package-info declares.
  @ArchTest
  static void modules(JavaClasses classes) {
    ApplicationModules.of(CoreApplication.class).verify();
  }

  // A controller calls a use case, a use case calls the rules and the repositories, and no call
  // goes back up.
  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule layers =
      layeredArchitecture()
          .consideringOnlyDependenciesInLayers()
          .layer("web")
          .definedBy("..internal.web..")
          .layer("app")
          .definedBy("..internal.app..")
          .layer("domain")
          .definedBy("..internal.domain..")
          .layer("data")
          .definedBy("..internal.data..")
          .whereLayer("web")
          .mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
          .whereLayer("app")
          .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("web")
          .whereLayer("data")
          .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("app")
          .whereLayer("domain")
          .mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("web", "app", "data");

  // A rule needs nothing of Spring nor of the other layers, so it runs and is tested on its own.
  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule pureDomain =
      classes()
          .that()
          .resideInAPackage("..internal.domain..")
          .should()
          .onlyDependOnClassesThat()
          .resideInAnyPackage("java..", "org.jspecify..", "..internal.domain..")
          .as("a rule should depend on nothing of Spring nor of the other layers");

  // A controller hands its work to a use case, so no rule of the domain runs in the web layer.
  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule noRuleInControllers =
      noClasses()
          .that()
          .resideInAPackage("..internal.web..")
          .should()
          .callCodeUnitWhere(target(owner(resideInAPackage("..internal.domain.."))))
          .as("a controller should call no rule");

  // A transaction starts in a use case alone, so the tenant is set where the use case begins.
  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule transactionsInUseCases =
      CompositeArchRule.of(
              noClasses()
                  .that()
                  .resideOutsideOfPackage("..internal.app..")
                  .should()
                  .beAnnotatedWith(Transactional.class))
          .and(
              noMethods()
                  .that()
                  .areDeclaredInClassesThat()
                  .resideOutsideOfPackage("..internal.app..")
                  .should()
                  .beAnnotatedWith(Transactional.class))
          .and(
              noClasses()
                  .that()
                  .resideOutsideOfPackages(
                      "..internal.app..", "dev.metis.core.platform.tenancy.internal..")
                  .should()
                  .dependOnClassesThat()
                  .belongToAnyOf(
                      TransactionTemplate.class,
                      TransactionOperations.class,
                      PlatformTransactionManager.class))
          .as("a transaction should start in a use case alone");

  // The person of a request reaches a module as a parameter, so no rule reads a static holder.
  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule noStaticHolder =
      noClasses()
          .that()
          .resideOutsideOfPackage("dev.metis.core.platform..")
          .should()
          .dependOnClassesThat()
          .belongToAnyOf(SecurityContextHolder.class, RequestContextHolder.class)
          .as("no module should read the person of a request from a static holder");

  // Spring makes every bean with what it needs, so code never makes one itself.
  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule noBeanMadeByHand =
      noClasses()
          .should()
          .callConstructorWhere(target(owner(metaAnnotatedWith(Component.class))))
          .as("no classes should make a bean with new");

  // Only a repository and the tenant hook reach the database, so no other code can run SQL.
  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule jdbcInRepositoriesAlone =
      noClasses()
          .that()
          .resideOutsideOfPackages(
              "..internal.data..", "dev.metis.core.platform.tenancy.internal..")
          .should()
          .dependOnClassesThat(JDBC)
          .as("only a repository and the tenant hook should reach the database");

  // A repository runs its statement and nothing more, so it hides no decision and builds no SQL.
  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule repositoriesRunTheirStatement =
      noClasses()
          .that()
          .resideInAPackage("..internal.data..")
          .should()
          .callCodeUnitWhere(
              DescribedPredicate.describe(
                  "anything but JdbcClient and the constructor of Object",
                  call ->
                      !STATEMENT.contains(call.getTargetOwner().getName())
                          && !(call.getTargetOwner().isEquivalentTo(Object.class)
                              && call.getName().equals("<init>"))))
          .as("a repository should call nothing but JdbcClient");

  // The text of every statement is a constant of its class, so no value is ever part of it.
  @ArchTest
  static void everyStatementIsAConstant(JavaClasses classes) throws IOException {
    List<String> found = new ArrayList<>();
    for (JavaClass type : classes) {
      found.addAll(statementsNotConstant(type));
    }
    assertThat(found).as("every statement should be a constant of its class").isEmpty();
  }

  // The methods of the class that call JdbcClient.sql with no string constant loaded just before.
  private static List<String> statementsNotConstant(JavaClass type) throws IOException {
    String file = type.getName().replace('.', '/') + ".class";
    byte[] bytes;
    try (InputStream in = ArchitectureTest.class.getClassLoader().getResourceAsStream(file)) {
      bytes = Objects.requireNonNull(in, file).readAllBytes();
    }
    List<String> found = new ArrayList<>();
    for (MethodModel method : ClassFile.of().parse(bytes).methods()) {
      Instruction before = null;
      for (CodeElement element : method.code().map(CodeModel::elementList).orElse(List.of())) {
        if (element instanceof InvokeInstruction call
            && call.owner()
                .asInternalName()
                .equals("org/springframework/jdbc/core/simple/JdbcClient")
            && call.name().equalsString("sql")
            && !(before instanceof ConstantInstruction.LoadConstantInstruction load
                && load.constantValue() instanceof String)) {
          found.add(type.getName() + "." + method.methodName().stringValue());
        }
        if (element instanceof Instruction instruction) {
          before = instruction;
        }
      }
    }
    return found;
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;

/** The counter-tests of the architecture check. */
final class ArchitectureCanaries {

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          Canary.of("architecture-field-injection", "architecture", "use field injection")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryInjected.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
                  import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
                  import org.springframework.core.env.Environment;
                  import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

                  @Component
                  final class CanaryInjected {
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** Every counter-test, in the order ./canary all runs them. */
public final class Canaries {

  /** The folder of the core's own classes, where most canaries plant a class. */
  static final String CORE = "core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/";

  /** Every counter-test, one list per check. */
  public static final List<Canary> ALL =
      Stream.of(
              FormatCanaries.ALL,
              CompileCanaries.ALL,
              LintCanaries.ALL,
              LanguageCanaries.ALL,
              ArchitectureCanaries.ALL,
              RepositoryCanaries.ALL,
              DeadcodeCanaries.ALL,
              ToolingCanaries.ALL,
              UnitCanaries.ALL,
              IntegrationCanaries.ALL,
              CoverageCanaries.ALL,
              MutationCanaries.ALL,
              DepsCanaries.ALL,
              SecretsCanaries.ALL,
              ImageCanaries.ALL)
          .flatMap(List::stream)
          .toList();

  private Canaries() {}
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;
import java.util.stream.IntStream;

/** The counter-tests of the lint check. */
final class LintCanaries {

  // Built from pieces, so that this file holds no mark of its own.
  private static final String SUPPRESS = "@Suppress" + "Warnings(\"unused\")";

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          // Ten branches over the one path of a method pass the ceiling of 10.
          Canary.of("lint-complexity", "lint", "[CyclomaticComplexity]")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryComplex.java",
                  classOf(
                      "CanaryComplex",
                      "  static int grade(int n) {\n"
                          + IntStream.range(0, 10)
                              .mapToObj(
                                  i ->
                                      "    if (n > %d) {\n      return %d;\n    }\n"
                                          .formatted(i, i))
                              .collect(Collectors.joining())
                          + "    return -1;\n  }\n")),
          // A file of 301 lines passes the ceiling of 300.
          Canary.of("lint-file-length", "lint", "[FileLength]")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryLong.java",
                  classOf(
                      "CanaryLong",
                      IntStream.range(0, 295)
                          .mapToObj(i -> "  static final int N%d = %d;\n".formatted(i, i))
                          .collect(Collectors.joining()))),
          Canary.of("lint-no-reason", "lint", "no-reason")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanarySuppressed.java",
                  classOf("CanarySuppressed", "  " + SUPPRESS + "\n  private int idle;\n")),
          // A mark with its reason still has to be counted in the debt file.
          Canary.of("lint-debt", "lint", "debt-grew")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryCounted.java",
                  classOf(
                      "CanaryCounted",
                      "  " + SUPPRESS + " // read by reflection\n  private int idle;\n")),
          // A mark on a parameter, which no line starts with.
          Canary.of("lint-parameter-suppression", "lint", "no-reason: static int twice(")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryParameter.java",
                  classOf(
                      "CanaryParameter",
                      "  static int twice("
                          + SUPPRESS
                          + " int number) {\n    return number * 2;\n  }\n")),
          // JaCoCo and PIT leave out a class so marked, so the mark is counted like the others.
          Canary.of("lint-generated", "lint", "debt-grew: 1 Generated")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryGenerated.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  @org.springframework.aot.generate.Generated
                  final class CanaryGenerated {
                    private CanaryGenerated() {}
                  }
                  """),
          // A mark in a package named like the record of ./verify, which only the root holds.
          Canary.of("lint-nested-reports", "lint", "reports/CanaryReports.java:6: no-reason")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "reports/CanaryReports.java",
                  classOf("CanaryReports", "  " + SUPPRESS + "\n  private int idle;\n")
                      .replace("package dev.metis.core;", "package dev.metis.core.reports;")),
          // A project whose every class the list leaves out, which would leave it unmeasured.
          Canary.of("lint-whole-project-excluded", "lint", "every class of extra is left out")
              .writing(
                  "extra/src/main/java/dev/metis/extra/Only.java",
                  "package dev.metis.extra;\n\nfinal class Only {}\n")
              .appending("config/coverage-exclusions.txt", "dev.metis.extra.Only: a canary\n"),
          // A repository that decides, which mutation testing would never see.
          Canary.of("lint-repository-decision", "lint", "(max allowed is 1)")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "workspace/internal/data/CanaryDecision.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core.workspace.internal.data;

                  final class CanaryDecision {
                    private CanaryDecision() {}

                    static int pick(boolean first) {
                      return first ? 1 : 2;
                    }
                  }
                  """),
          Canary.of("lint-mutation-exclusion", "lint", "no-reason: dev.metis.core.CoreApplication")
              .appending("config/mutation-exclusions.txt", "dev.metis.core.CoreApplication\n"));

  private LintCanaries() {}

  // A class of the core with the body given, and a private constructor before it.
  private static String classOf(String name, String body) {
    return """
        package dev.metis.core;

        final class %s {
          private %s() {}

        %s}
        """
        .formatted(name, name, body);
  }
}
```

### Task 9: The README and the AGENTS file

The README says what the repository holds now, how to run the integration tests and how to run the local stack by hand, with its four passwords in a file outside the repository, where git never sees them and the secret scan of `./verify` never reads them. AGENTS.md gives an agent the rules of the modules, the repositories, the migrations, the exclusions from mutation testing and the test sets.

**Files:**

- Modify: `README.md`
- Modify: `AGENTS.md`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: everything above.
- Produces: the files `README.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

```markdown
# metis-backend

The Metis backend: the business core (roles `api` and `worker`), the MCP gateway, the AI agent, the
Keycloak extensions and the sandbox images, built by the backend team. Today it holds the Gradle
build, the core with its platform module and the first read, `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/shell`,
served from PostgreSQL behind a token with tenants kept apart by the database, the local stack that
runs it as a deployment does, and the tool that runs every check and records the run.

Its documentation lives in the `metis-docs` repository: `architecture/` for how the parts fit and why,
and `components/core/`, `components/mcp-gateway/`, `components/agent/`, `components/keycloak/` and
`components/sandbox/` for each part.

## What a machine needs

Docker, and any JDK from 17 on to start Gradle, found through `JAVA_HOME` or the path. Gradle runs
itself and the build on Amazon Corretto 25, which it downloads on its first run. The integration
tests start PostgreSQL and Keycloak in Docker through Testcontainers.

## Commands

- `./verify` runs every check in order, goes on after a red one, and writes `reports/verify.json`
  and `reports/verify.md`; it exits 1 when a check is red.
- `./verify --fast` runs the fast group, the checks from format to unit, the set CI runs on every
  push.
- `./verify --only lint,unit --append` reruns some checks and adds their rows to the record.
- `./canary all` plants one defect per counter-test in a copy of the tree under `build/canary/` and
  requires each check to go red for it; `./canary lint-complexity` runs one.
- `./gradlew checkLint` runs one check; the checks are the tasks named `check` and a capital in
  `build.gradle.kts`.
- `docker build --file core/Dockerfile --tag metis-core:local .` builds the image from the sources.
- `./gradlew :core:integrationTest` runs the tests on a real PostgreSQL and a real Keycloak.

## The local stack

`stack/compose.yaml` starts PostgreSQL, Keycloak with the development realm of
`stack/keycloak/metis.json`, the migration job and then the API, each waiting for what it needs. It
reads four passwords from the environment and holds none: `METIS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`,
`METIS_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD`, `METIS_APP_PASSWORD` and `METIS_PERSON_PASSWORD`, the password of the
people of the realm: `developer`, and `two-tenants`, whose token names two tenants and is answered
401. Keep the passwords in a file outside the repository, at a path you choose, and name that path
in `METIS_STACK_ENV`. The secret scan of `./verify` reads every file of the tree, the ones git
ignores included, so a file of passwords inside it turns the scan red. With `METIS_STACK_ENV` set:

~~~sh
for name in POSTGRES MIGRATOR APP PERSON; do echo "METIS_${name}_PASSWORD=$(uuidgen)"; done > "$METIS_STACK_ENV"
docker compose --env-file "$METIS_STACK_ENV" --file stack/compose.yaml up --build --wait
docker compose --env-file "$METIS_STACK_ENV" --file stack/compose.yaml down --volumes
~~~

`--build` builds the image from the sources first; without it the stack runs whatever image
`metis-core:local` names, an older build included. The API answers on `127.0.0.1:8080`, or on the
port `METIS_PORT` gives. A token for the person of the realm comes from Keycloak inside the stack,
whose address is the issuer the API trusts:

~~~sh
docker compose --env-file "$METIS_STACK_ENV" --file stack/compose.yaml exec core \
  curl --silent --data grant_type=password --data client_id=metis-dev --data username=developer \
  --data-urlencode "password=$(grep PERSON "$METIS_STACK_ENV" | cut -d= -f2)" \
  http://keycloak:8080/realms/metis/protocol/openid-connect/token
~~~
```

`AGENTS.md`:

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

Instructions for AI coding agents working in `metis-backend`.

## Read first

The documentation lives in the `metis-docs` repository, cloned beside this one as `../metis-docs`.
Read, in this order:

1. `../metis-docs/llms.txt`: the index of every current page.
2. `../metis-docs/architecture/overview.md`, then the folder under `../metis-docs/components/` of the
   part you work on: `core`, `mcp-gateway`, `agent`, `keycloak` or `sandbox`.
3. `../metis-docs/AGENTS.md` before you change any documentation.

`.claude/settings.json` lists `../metis-docs` under `permissions.additionalDirectories`. Once the
owner's probe confirms that Claude Code resolves that relative path from this folder, it reads the
clone without asking, after you accept the trust dialog for this folder. Until then, and wherever
it asks anyway, each developer adds the absolute path of their clone under the same key in
`.claude/settings.local.json`, which git ignores.

## Rules

- The pages about the backend that describe what is not built yet are drafts. Read the decision
  records in `../metis-docs/architecture/decisions/` before you choose a library or a pattern.
- Code, comments, test names, log messages and tool output are English. A letter outside ASCII is
  allowed only on the line after a `lang-exception` comment that gives its reason after the colon,
  and `./gradlew checkLanguage` rejects any other.
- A comment is one line that says why. It never names a plan, a ruling, a task, a date or a line of
  another file. A deliberate shortcut says `ponytail: <its ceiling>; <how to lift it>`.
- Every escape hatch gives its reason and is counted in `config/debt.json`: a suppressed warning,
  a method left out of mutation testing, an annotation whose name holds `Generated` (JaCoCo and PIT
  leave out what it marks), an excused line of the language check, a class left out of coverage in
  `config/coverage-exclusions.txt`, a class left out of mutation testing in
  `config/mutation-exclusions.txt`. A walk entry in `config/entry-points.txt` gives its reason too.
- The core is modules of Spring Modulith: `platform` (named interfaces `web` and `security`) and
  `workspace`. A module is a package under `dev.metis.core` whose `package-info.java` lists the
  modules it may use; it keeps its code under `internal/web`, `internal/app`, `internal/domain` and
  `internal/data`. A controller calls a use case; a use case, the only place a transaction starts,
  calls the rules of `domain` and the repositories of `data`; `domain` uses nothing of Spring.
- A repository runs SQL written as a text block with named parameters through `JdbcClient` and
  makes no decision: `./gradlew checkLint` holds its methods to a complexity of 1, and
  `./gradlew checkArchitecture` holds the text of every statement to a constant of its class, lets
  a repository call nothing but `JdbcClient`, and lets no class but a repository and the tenant
  hook reach the database. Repositories and the transaction manager that sets the tenant are the
  two entries of `config/mutation-exclusions.txt`; the integration tests prove them.
- A new table comes in a new migration under `core/src/main/resources/db/migration`, with the tenant
  column and its default, row-level security enabled and forced, the one policy on the tenant of the
  transaction, and the grants the code uses; the catalog test of the integration check reads the
  database and fails a table that misses any of them. A migration never creates a role and never
  changes once merged.
- Tests that need no container are in `core/src/test`; tests on a real PostgreSQL and a real
  Keycloak are in `core/src/integrationTest` and read the stack's own files; what both share is in
  `core/src/testShared`. A test that proves a requirement opens its `@DisplayName` with its BRD id,
  and the language check reads the title as it reads a comment.
- The number of tests that pass equals `test-floor.json`, so a change that adds or removes tests
  updates it; no test is skipped or disabled.
- Never edit what a command writes: `gradlew`, `gradle/wrapper/`, `gradle/gradle-daemon-jvm.properties`,
  the `gradle.lockfile` files and `gradle/verification-metadata.xml`. After a change of the
  dependencies, write the locks and the checksums again, with every task run for real, since a task
  restored from the build cache resolves nothing:
  `./gradlew --refresh-dependencies --write-locks --write-verification-metadata sha256 --rerun-tasks help spotlessCheck :core:checkLicense`.
- A new check is a task named `check` and a capital in the root `build.gradle.kts` and a row of
  `Checks.ORDER` in the tool, in the order of the spec; `./verify` refuses a check task the list
  lacks, in whatever project it is registered. It has its counter-test in
  `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/` or its reason in the `NoCanary` table of the
  tool's tests, and `./gradlew checkTooling` fails a check that has neither. Its judge leaves
  facts in `build/facts/`, or the check fails, unless the root build names it in `factFree`.
- No project declares a library that a bundle of the root build names: a bundle stands for its
  starter, so a library it names is never reported unused, and `./gradlew checkDeadcode` refuses
  the declaration.
- Before you hand work back, run the fast checks, the set CI runs on every push: `./verify --fast`.
- A change of behaviour needs its documentation change in `metis-docs`.
```

The test floor moved from architecture 14, integration 54, tooling 176 and unit 66 to 17, 58, 180 and 76, and `./canary all` from 81 counter-tests to 96.

The rulings on the four questions of the writer's report:

- `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` stays public: it names the issuer alone, which every token and Keycloak's own discovery already publish, and MCP clients will need it.
- An encoded slash answers 400 with kind `validation`, and 405, 406 and 415 keep the kind `validation`, until a client needs to tell them apart.
- A `GenericContainer` of the stack's own Keycloak image is accepted in place of `testcontainers-keycloak`; the controller corrects the spec.
- Plan four makes the realm's person the demo person of the app's fixtures, with the subject and the tenant of the demo seed; nothing changes now.

The test floor moved to architecture 18 and tooling 182, and `./canary all` from 96 counter-tests to 104. The record of the round: `./verify` read every row green on one tree, `7a5919cab5b4`, and 46 of the 46 counter-tests of `architecture`, `mutation` and `integration` went red because of their planted defect.

## Trial run in the sandbox

On 15 Oct 2026, on the owner's Mac (arm64, ten cores, 24 GiB; macOS on Darwin 25.6.0; Docker Desktop 29.4.3 with ten processors and 7.75 GiB; Homebrew's OpenJDK 21 starting Gradle 9.8.1 on Corretto 25.0.4.10.1), plan two was built test-first in a copy of `metis-backend` as plan one left it, its `.git` included, and its review round one was fixed there. Then every task of this page, as it stands after that round, was replayed in a second fresh copy made from plan one's snapshot, `.work/snaps/metis-backend-plan-one-8394963fa222.tgz`, step by step, by a script that wrote the whole-file blocks and ran the commands, in one run from Task 1 to the `./verify` of Task 10. Each Expected block above is that replay's own output, with the path of the copy written as `metis-backend`, except the `./canary all` of Task 10: the controller's change of method for the round stopped the replay's run after 92 of the 93 counter-tests it had started had gone red because of their planted defect, the last one cut short, so that block is the run of `metis-backend` itself. Finally the page was extracted with `extract-plan.py` into an empty folder and compared with the sandbox, file by file with `cmp`, by `compare.sh` in the owner's work folder, whose last line read: "extracted 137 files (3 written then deleted by a later task): 0 differ, 0 changes of the sandbox missing from the plan". The lock files and the checksums are generated, so the comparison leaves them out.
