## What the sandbox taught

- The Keycloak module of Testcontainers (`testcontainers-keycloak` 4.4.0, which the spec names) brings the admin client of Keycloak, with Jackson 2.21.5, in which Trivy finds CVE-2026-89407 (HIGH) and CVE-2026-68497, so `checkDeps` refuses it. A `GenericContainer` of the stack's own image of Keycloak, with the realm copied in and a wait on the discovery page, does the same work with no library added.
- The configurations of a new source set start without the platforms of the conventions. Symptom: Trivy found Jackson 3.1.5 and Tomcat 11.0.24 in the lock file again, from the configurations of the integration tests. Fix: they extend `implementation` and `runtimeOnly`, as the unit tests do.
- `test-support` holds the architecture rules, which need ArchUnit; the source set of the integration tests leaves that file out.
- Keycloak's import of a realm replaces `${METIS_PERSON_PASSWORD}` with the variable of the environment: the literal placeholder as a password gave `invalid_grant`, the value of the variable gave a token. The realm declares no user profile, and the attribute still reaches the token through its mapper (`KeycloakTest` and the image check read the shell with 200); a user without an email, a first and a last name is refused as "Account is not fully set up". The image of Keycloak has no curl: the health check asks the management port 9000 through bash's `/dev/tcp`.
- The issuer of a token is the address it was asked at. The API reaches Keycloak as `http://keycloak:8080` inside the stack, so the image check asks for its token from inside the stack, through `docker exec` in the container of the core, which has curl.
- Keys of the issuer that cannot be read make `SupplierJwtDecoder` throw `JwtDecoderInitializationException` ("Failed to lazily resolve the supplied JwtDecoder instance", caused by "Connection refused"), which is no bad token, so it left the filters of Spring Security unanswered: measured by running `SecurityTest` with the decoder unwrapped, where MockMvc reported "Request failed unexpectedly". The decoder of the core turns any failure to read the keys into `BadJwtException`, which answers 401. Spring Security 7 also names `resource_metadata` in `WWW-Authenticate` and serves `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` to anyone, claiming tokens bound to client certificates; its configurer can only change the metadata, so the core makes it name the issuer and claim no binding.
- Tomcat 11 refuses an encoded slash in a path with an HTML page of its own, without Problem Details and without `no-store`. Fix: the connector passes it through, the firewall of Spring Security refuses it, and the error page of the core answers 400 as Problem Details.
- Spring Boot's test filter leaves out a `@RestController` nested in a test class; such a controller is imported.
- Spring's cache of test contexts hid mutants of bean methods from PIT: a mutant that changes a bean method ran against a context built under an earlier mutant, so it survived. Fix: the web-layer tests start a context per class, `@DirtiesContext(classMode = BEFORE_CLASS)`, and the decoder is a static function a unit test calls with the keys of the test issuer.
- PIT keeps a mutant of `a || b` alive when no test separates the two conditions; the refusal of the image check and the read of a token each got the case that does, or lost the condition no case needed.
- ArchUnit does not see a join of strings, which javac compiles to `invokedynamic`; the core's classes compile with `-XDstringConcat=inline`, so a join is calls of `StringBuilder`, which the rule against SQL from strings refuses in a repository.
- Mockito attaches itself to a JVM of JDK 25 at run time, with warnings that a later JDK will refuse it; it joins every test JVM and PIT's as `-javaagent` from a configuration of its own.
- Flyway needs a second connection while it holds one, so a pool of one stopped the start (`Connection is not available, request timed out after 30120ms (total=1, active=1, idle=0, waiting=0)`). The test of a pooled connection relies on HikariCP handing a thread the connection it used last, and proves it by the process id of the connection on both sides.
- PostgreSQL leaves an empty text, not null, in a setting a transaction made local once the transaction ends: measured in `TenantTransactionTest`, which settles what the spec marked unverified; the policy reads both as no tenant.
- `SpringApplication.withHook` hooks every start inside its action: the shared database, migrated by the migration job, starts first, or the hook sees the job before the API. `OutputCaptureExtension` captures from before the test, the plain lines of the containers included, so the tests of the log read the output from a mark.
- `docker compose up --wait` without `--build` runs whatever image `metis-core:local` names: plan one's, an empty web application, so the migration job never ended and the stack kept waiting until it was stopped.
- The secret scan reads a local file of passwords in the tree (`leaks found: 4` for four values made by `uuidgen`), and its allow-list may not grow, so the README keeps the file outside the repository.
- The sandbox only ever holds the last tree, so a file that a task writes before its first user passes there and fails in the replay. The first replay stopped at the `./verify` of Task 3 on three findings of the deadcode check: `UserToken.serialVersionUID`, `CurrentUser.subject()` and the method of the unit test of the probes that gives Spring the address of the issuer. The walk had passed `serialVersionUID` only because four classes name it by the end, and a final constant counts as read when its name appears twice; it now knows that the serialization of the JDK reads it in a serializable class. It now also knows what the test context of Spring calls, such as a method marked `@DynamicPropertySource`. And `Authentication.getName()` gave `CurrentUser[subject=subject, tenant=0b0e5a4e-7c5a-4f43-9d7e-1f2a3b4c5d6e]`, the tenant included, so the token names the person by the subject alone, which reads `subject()` from Task 3 on. Since then every tree a task leaves is built in a scratch copy and passes `./verify --fast` before a replay starts.
- The second replay stopped at the counter-test lint-mutation-exclusion of Task 5: it expected its planted entry on line 5 of `config/mutation-exclusions.txt`, which holds only once Task 6 adds the second entry, and found `config/mutation-exclusions.txt:4: no-reason: dev.metis.core.CoreApplication`. It now expects the finding without its line, which also holds when a later plan adds an entry.
- The PostgreSQL module of Testcontainers 2.0.5 waits for its log line `database system is ready to accept connections` and never connects (`javap` of `PostgreSQLContainer`). The first apply to `metis-backend` stopped at the `./verify` of Task 6: in the run of the integration tests the coverage check makes, `StartupTest` met "Connection to localhost:53334 refused" 0.1 s after the module called the container started, while the log of Docker Desktop shows its forwarder listening on that port before then. The image itself listens on TCP before its second "ready" line, and 25 starts of it by hand, each with a connection at once, all connected, so the cause inside Docker Desktop is not proven. `Stack.database()` now waits for a first connection; `metis-backend` went back to plan one's snapshot and the apply ran again from Task 1.
- Awaitility runs a condition in a thread of its own. The first database is made while `Stack` initializes, and a condition that calls a static method of `Stack` waits for that initialization, which waits for the condition: "Condition with Lambda expression in dev.metis.core.Stack was not fulfilled within 1 minutes", caused by a `TimeoutException`, and every class of the integration tests failed. `pollInSameThread()` runs the condition in the calling thread.
- The step of the image check that requires the API alone to refuse an unmigrated database read the state of the container as soon as the readiness probe ended, and the probe ends with the process of the core, while its container can still read `running`. The replay after the guard of `Stack.database()` caught 80 of 81 defects: image-root was "already red before planting", its unplanted run reporting `the API did not refuse a database no migration job ran on: running 0` under a log that ends in `Application run failed`. The check now stops the container, within the stack's grace of 30 seconds, before it reads the state; a container that already exited keeps its own exit code, and Flyway's line in the log still names the reason.
- `ShutdownTest`, from plan one, waited without a limit for its held request to reach the endpoint. In a later replay, under the counter-test integration-session-tenant, the request was answered before it got there: a dump of every thread, virtual ones included, showed none in `hold()` and the HTTP client idle, and the test JVM waited eleven minutes until it was stopped. The same order of tests, rerun with its seed, passed, so the early answer is a race whose cause is not proven. The wait now ends after 20 seconds, and its failure names the answer.
- Gradle keeps the checksum of a library no configuration resolves any more: the sandbox's `gradle/verification-metadata.xml` still held 99 entries of the Keycloak module of Testcontainers, dropped days before, so its tree differed from the replay's in that file alone. The sandbox took the replay's file, which the commands of this page write from plan one's, and `./verify` then read the tree of the replay's Task 10.
- `extract-plan.py` ends a whole-file block at the first line that opens with three backticks, so a README with fenced commands came out cut; the README fences its commands with `~~~`.
- Keycloak's attribute mapper set to multivalued sends every value as a list, one value too: with it, the token of `developer` named its one tenant as a list of one, and the core answered it 401. The core now takes a list of one UUID as that tenant, and a list of two, the case a single-valued mapper would have narrowed to its first value, stays 401.
- Hikari's `data-source-properties` is a `java.util.Properties`, which the test of the settings did not read as a map: `logServerErrorDetail` came out as a setting nothing binds. The test now reads a `Properties` as Spring Boot binds it, key by key.
- `docker compose up --wait-timeout 5`, without `--wait`, gives up on a dependency that never completes: "timeout waiting for dependencies", exit 1 after 6 s, measured with Docker Compose 5.1.4, so the image check bounds the start of the stack without waiting for the health of the core.
- Gradle refuses to store this build in its configuration cache ("cannot serialize Gradle script object references" for `:core:test`), so a run with `--configuration-cache` configures anew and printed its own seed each time (3675067196783583, then 3675076312066166). A build made fit for that cache would keep the seed it stored.
- PIT runs many mutants in one worker, one after the other. The mutant that removed `MDC.remove` left the tenant on the thread, and the mutant that removed `MDC.put` then survived, since the test read the value left over. The test of the filter now starts each case with an empty MDC.
- In one command with `--continue`, a unit test of the core that did not compile left `:core:integrationTest` and `:tools:test` unrun, and the build failed in 1 s; Task 5 therefore sees its tests fail in two steps.
- On macOS a program bound to `127.0.0.1` takes the traffic of that address before a program bound to every address on the same port, and both Docker Desktop and a listener that sets `SO_REUSEADDR` may bind such a port. Measured with the probes `shadow_probe.py` and `alloc_probe.py` in the owner's work folder: a listener on `127.0.0.1` at a port, then a container published there by Docker Desktop on every address, `docker run` exit 0; a connection to `127.0.0.1` reached the listener, not PostgreSQL; in the other order, PostgreSQL answered the first connection and the listener the next; published on `127.0.0.1` alone, the container failed to start ("bind: address already in use"). Docker Desktop takes its port from the same sequence as the Mac's own (54239 the Mac's, 54240 Docker's, 54241 the Mac's), and the Gradle daemons hold about ten ports of that range on `127.0.0.1`. Two replays met it. In one `./canary all`, the unplanted run of integration-bypassrls got 401 with the body "auth required", which the core never sends: another program answered the port of a core that listened on every address. In the next replay, the unplanted run of integration-tree-order failed `StartupTest`: the first connection to a new database ended with `EOFException` during the request for TLS, for the whole minute of the wait, an answer PostgreSQL never gives. The cores of the tests now listen on `127.0.0.1` alone and the containers of the tests publish there alone, where the system gives a port that is free on that address; `StackTest` requires it of the shared database. The early answer that once held `ShutdownTest` fits the same cause. Testcontainers' own container, Ryuk, still publishes on every address; see "Left for plan three".
- Inside a task block of the Kotlin DSL, `java` is the extension of the project, so `java.time.Duration` does not resolve; the build imports `java.time.Duration` instead.
- The first `./canary all` of the sandbox caught 76 of 81 defects. coverage-unit-only failed for another reason: its replacement in the build of the core broke the test of the counter-tests inside the copy, so it appends. image-compose-writable, image-compose-root and image-compose-capability passed: the migration job, first in the compose file, took the plants meant for the core, so the core comes first. integration-exposed-endpoint went red for a wrong reason: a second `management:` key appended to `application.yml` broke the YAML and every test, so it replaces into the existing key, and only the test of the discovery page fails.
- The refusal of an unmigrated database passed when the API stopped for any reason, so in image-root-write, whose API stopped on its write to a read-only root, the refusal passed and the check went red later, at the migration job, without the line the counter-test looks for; it now requires Flyway's own message in the log of the core, and prints the last lines of that log otherwise.

## Left for plan three

- The rule of the deadcode check on a table, a column or a resource file nothing names: the tables hold only the columns the shell reads, so plan three adds the rest of `workspace`, `person` and `project` by a new migration and builds the rule with its first leftover in view.
- The profile `demo`, with its fixed date, arrives with the demo data; `test` needs no file of its own.
- The schema of a badge: `Nav.Item.badge` is a `Void`, always null, until the focus list and the approval queue count; the contract of plan three needs its type.
- `ProjectRegistry`, the interface of `workspace` that `delivery` will call.
- `@DoNotMutate`: still no method needs it.
- A name or initials may be empty in the database, while the app requires one letter at least: the contract of plan three carries `minLength: 1` from the app's schema, and its migration adds `check (column <> '')` to those columns.
- The demo data of plan four reaches the database either as a Flyway callback, which the history does not record, or with the API ignoring `*:missing`; a case of `StartupTest` proves the layout chosen.
- The time limit of the weekly job of CI is measured on its first run, then the job is split by check or its limit raised.
- The two races bounded without a proven cause. The connection refused to a new database 0.1 s after its start, which `Stack.database()` waits out, is no case of a shared port, since a refused connection means no program listened at all. The held request of `ShutdownTest` answered before its endpoint fits another program on the same port, which the tests now rule out, and its wait still fails after 20 seconds with the answer.
- Ryuk, the container with which Testcontainers removes the others, publishes its port on every address, and Testcontainers offers no setting to change it (`javap` of Testcontainers 2.0.5: its settings of Ryuk are the image, the privileged mode and the timeout), so on macOS a program on `127.0.0.1` at that port would stop a run of the integration tests ("Could not connect to Ryuk"); none did in the replays.
- The rule that `platform` code has two users, which needs the second business module.
- What section 2 of the brief leaves to plans three and four: the module `delivery`, `project_member`, `wbs_node` and the overview; the contract and the checks `contract` and `trace`; the demo data and the restated-literal rule; the relay; calls generated from the contract, the latency budget and the stop during a slow request.
